method: The authors generalize q-plate state generation and characterization to arbitrary topological charges and detuning, showing that the exchange Berry phase acts as a geometric marker governing spatial interference patterns.
result: The Berry phase enables deterministic control and reveals topological invariants and phase singularities that serve as a non-tomographic witness for state dimensionality estimation.
conclusion: This device-independent and scalable approach enables high-dimensional characterization and topologically protected state selection, with applications in quantum metrology and quantum networks.

title: Louvre: Relaxing Hardware Requirements Of Quantum Ldpc Codes By Routing With Expanded Quantum Instruction Set
authors: Runshi Zhou
Fang Zhang
Hui-Hai Zhao
Feng Wu
Linghang Kong
Jianxin Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a routing-based approach to relax hardware connectivity requirements for quantum LDPC codes using an expanded quantum instruction set.
motivation: Quantum LDPC codes promise low overhead but require high connectivity, which is challenging for near-term hardware. This work aims to reduce connectivity demands by introducing routing operations.
method: The authors design an expanded quantum instruction set that includes routing operations, enabling the implementation of LDPC codes on hardware with limited connectivity. They analyze the trade-offs between routing overhead and code performance.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces the required hardware connectivity for implementing quantum LDPC codes, with manageable overhead in terms of additional gates and time.
conclusion: Routing with an expanded instruction set is a practical approach to make quantum LDPC codes feasible on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum error correction implementation.

title: Entanglement As A Fairness Mechanism In Randomized Quantum Games
authors: Ri-Hua Zheng
Yang Xiao
Ye-Hong Chen
Zhi-Cheng Shi
Yan Xia
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes using entanglement as a fairness mechanism in randomized quantum games, showing that entangled strategies can enforce fairness in competitive settings.
motivation: Classical randomized games often suffer from unfair advantages due to imperfect randomness or cheating. The authors aim to leverage quantum entanglement to guarantee fairness without trusted third parties.
method: They design a quantum game where players share entangled states and perform measurements; the game's outcome is determined by quantum correlations, ensuring that no player can bias the result unilaterally.
result: The entangled protocol achieves provable fairness, outperforming classical randomization in terms of resistance to cheating and efficiency.
conclusion: Entanglement can serve as a practical resource for fairness in multi-party protocols, with potential applications in quantum cryptography and distributed computing.

title: Bootstrapping Quantum Hamiltonians With Symmetry
authors: Michael G. Scheer
abstract:
Author(s): Michael G. Scheer

We describe a semidefinite relaxation method which finds lower bounds to the ground state energy of a quantum Hamiltonian subject to Hermitian linear constraints along with approximations of ground state expectation values. We show that symmetry can be used to significantly reduce the computational …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246501] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A semidefinite relaxation method for bounding ground state energies of quantum Hamiltonians using symmetry reduction.
motivation: Computing ground state energies of quantum Hamiltonians is hard; symmetry can reduce complexity.
method: Formulates a semidefinite program that incorporates Hermitian linear constraints and symmetry to obtain lower bounds and approximate expectation values.
result: Demonstrates that symmetry significantly reduces computational cost while maintaining tight bounds.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool for studying quantum many-body systems with symmetries.

title: State- Versus Reaction-Based Information Processing In Biochemical Networks
authors: Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein Ten Wolde, And Christoph Zechner
abstract:
Author(s): Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein ten Wolde, and Christoph Zechner

Trajectory mutual information is frequently used to quantify information transfer in biochemical systems. Tractable solutions of the trajectory mutual information can be obtained via the widely used linear-noise approximation (LNA) using Gaussian channel theory. This approach is expected to be accur…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248401] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes information processing in biochemical networks using trajectory mutual information and the linear-noise approximation, connecting to thermodynamic constraints.
motivation: Understanding how biochemical networks process information is crucial for systems biology, and the trajectory mutual information is a key measure that can be linked to thermodynamic costs.
method: The authors use the linear-noise approximation (LNA) to compute trajectory mutual information in biochemical networks, treating the system as a Gaussian channel.
result: They find that the LNA-based Gaussian channel approach accurately captures information transfer in certain regimes, and they derive bounds relating information to thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for quantifying information processing in biochemical systems and highlights the role of thermodynamics in setting limits on information transfer.

title: Parent Hamiltonians For Stabilizer Quantum Many-Body Scars
authors: Shane Dooley
abstract:
Author(s): Shane Dooley

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) have attracted considerable interest due to their role in weak ergodicity breaking in many-body systems. We present a general construction that embeds stabilizer states as QMBS of local Hamiltonians. The method relies on a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings on …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240402] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A general construction to embed stabilizer states as quantum many-body scars in local Hamiltonians.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars provide a mechanism for weak ergodicity breaking, and embedding stabilizer states as scars could enable controlled non-thermal behavior.
method: The construction uses factorizability of Pauli strings to design parent Hamiltonians whose eigenstates include stabilizer states as scars.
result: Stabilizer states can be realized as exact eigenstates (scars) of local Hamiltonians, with the method generalizing to any stabilizer state.
conclusion: This work provides a systematic way to embed known quantum states into scarred spectra, potentially useful for quantum information tasks like state preparation.

title: Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics With $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry-related Asymmetric Transparency
authors: Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, And Kashif Ammar Yasir
abstract:
Author(s): Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, and Kashif Ammar Yasir

We investigate magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling. The setup consists of a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere, where the magnon mode is further hybridized w…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063522] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with non-Hermitian coupling and PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian effects and PT-symmetry in hybrid quantum systems, specifically cavity magnomechanics, which may enable novel control of light-matter interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling, using input-output formalism to study transparency and asymmetry.
result: Demonstrates asymmetric transparency windows arising from PT-symmetry breaking, with potential for sensing and switching applications.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian cavity magnomechanics offers a platform for studying PT-symmetry and asymmetric responses, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and quantum information processing.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In An Asymmetrical Cavity
authors: Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, and Yaping Yang

Inspired by the distinctive properties of universal photon blockade (UPB), we propose a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve quantum nonreciprocity. Through theoretical analysis, we establish direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB in weak-driving limita…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063729] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve nonreciprocal universal photon blockade, enabling quantum nonreciprocity.
motivation: Universal photon blockade (UPB) is a key effect for single-photon sources and quantum information processing, but achieving nonreciprocal behavior is challenging. The authors aim to realize direction-dependent photon blockade using an asymmetrical cavity.
method: They theoretically analyze a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity, deriving optimal conditions for perfect UPB under weak driving. The asymmetry is introduced via different cavity couplings or detunings for forward and backward propagation.
result: They find that perfect UPB can be achieved in one direction while being suppressed in the opposite direction, leading to nonreciprocal photon blockade. The conditions depend on the asymmetry parameters.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a route to realize quantum nonreciprocity at the single-photon level, which is useful for quantum networks and chiral quantum optics.

title: Effects Of Static Dc Electric-field Orientation On Two-photon Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas Destefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, And Irina Novikova
abstract:
Author(s): Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas DeStefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, and Irina Novikova

We examine the influence of a static dc electric field on electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances that involve highly excited Rydberg states. Our focus is on how these resonances are altered when the relative orientation between the laser polarization and the external electric-fiel…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062619] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the orientation of a static DC electric field relative to laser polarization affects two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances.
motivation: Understanding the influence of electric field orientation on Rydberg EIT is important for applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems where Rydberg atoms are coupled to other platforms.
method: The authors experimentally measure EIT spectra in a Rydberg atomic vapor cell while varying the angle between the DC electric field and the laser polarization, and compare with theoretical models.
result: They find that the EIT resonance amplitude and linewidth depend strongly on the field orientation, consistent with Stark shift and transition dipole moment calculations.
conclusion: The orientation of the DC field must be carefully controlled for precise Rydberg EIT-based measurements and for optimizing hybrid quantum interfaces.

title: Application And Quantum Properties Of Superpositions Of Oppositely Squeezed States
authors: Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, and Kae Nemoto

We show that superpositions of oppositely squeezed states—non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states—exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime. These states possess photon-number structures distinct from conventional coherent-state cat s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063728] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are shown to have enhanced nonclassical features and entanglement advantages in the small-squeezing regime.
motivation: To explore non-Gaussian states beyond conventional cat states for quantum information applications.
method: The authors construct superpositions of oppositely squeezed states and analyze their photon-number statistics, nonclassicality, and entanglement properties.
result: These states exhibit stronger nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime compared to standard cat states.
conclusion: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are promising resources for quantum information processing, especially in regimes where squeezing is limited.

title: Optimal Control Of Open-quantum-system Dynamics Predicted By Long Short-term Memory
authors: Jun-Dong Zhong And Zhao-Ming Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Dong Zhong and Zhao-Ming Wang

The realization of high-fidelity quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, particularly in noisy environments where control strategies must simultaneously achieve precise manipulation and effective noise suppression. Conventional optimal control designs typically require numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062442] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Uses long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to predict optimal control pulses for open quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity control in noisy environments.
motivation: Conventional optimal control for open quantum systems is computationally expensive; machine learning offers a faster alternative for predicting control strategies.
method: Trains an LSTM network on data from optimal control solutions (e.g., GRAPE) to predict control pulses for given system parameters and noise conditions.
result: The LSTM-based approach predicts control pulses with high fidelity, significantly reducing computation time compared to traditional numerical optimization.
conclusion: Machine learning, specifically LSTM, can efficiently predict optimal quantum control in open systems, aiding practical quantum information processing.

title: Enhancing Collective Spin Squeezing Via One-axis-twisting Echo Control Of Individual Atoms
authors: Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, And Yanhong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, and Yanhong Xiao

Spin squeezing generated via interatom entanglement in multilevel atomic ensembles provides a powerful resource for quantum-enhanced metrology. Existing schemes that harness internal atomic degrees of freedom to boost squeezing typically encode the collective squeezing in complex superpositions of m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062809] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a one-axis-twisting echo control scheme to enhance collective spin squeezing in multilevel atomic ensembles, improving metrological gain.
motivation: Existing spin squeezing schemes using internal atomic degrees of freedom suffer from limited squeezing due to decoherence and complexity. The authors aim to develop a simpler and more robust method to boost squeezing.
method: They introduce a one-axis-twisting echo control technique that applies a sequence of pulses to individual atoms in a multilevel ensemble, effectively refocusing inhomogeneous broadening and enhancing entanglement.
result: The proposed scheme achieves significantly higher spin squeezing compared to standard one-axis-twisting, with improved robustness against dephasing and experimental imperfections.
conclusion: This echo control approach provides a practical and effective way to generate strong spin squeezing in atomic ensembles, advancing quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Increasing Entanglement Concentration And The Role Of Measurement Imaginarity
authors: Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, And Debasis Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, and Debasis Sarkar

The role of complex numbers in quantum theory extends beyond mathematical convenience, having recently been formalized as a resource under the framework of the resource theory of imaginarity. Operationally, imaginarity translates into using more resources in linear optical setups. In this work, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062439] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how measurement imaginarity (a resource in quantum theory) can enhance entanglement concentration, showing that complex measurements outperform real ones.
motivation: To understand the operational role of complex numbers in quantum theory, specifically whether measurement imaginarity can improve entanglement distillation protocols.
method: The authors develop a resource-theoretic framework for measurement imaginarity and apply it to entanglement concentration protocols, comparing the performance of real vs. complex measurements.
result: They find that using measurements with non-zero imaginarity can increase the success probability or yield of entanglement concentration, demonstrating a quantum advantage.
conclusion: Measurement imaginarity is a useful resource for entanglement manipulation, and its exploitation can lead to more efficient entanglement concentration.

title: Demonstration Of The Universal Intrinsic Higher-rank Spin Tensor Hall Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, And Yiheng Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, and Yiheng Lin

The spin Hall effect enables pure spin-current generation without charge transport. Notably, its intrinsic contribution, originating from spin-orbit coupling, can exhibit universal values that are robust against parameter fluctuations. Recent extensions of this effect to high-spin systems predict ri…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062616] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect using a trapped ion system.
motivation: To extend the spin Hall effect to high-spin systems and demonstrate universal behavior robust against parameter fluctuations.
method: Trapped ion platform used to simulate higher-rank spin tensors and measure the Hall effect.
result: Observed universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Trapped ions provide a versatile platform for studying higher-rank spin transport phenomena.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics system to generate n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve tunable bundle emissions of phonons and photon-phonon pairs, which are important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses the Barnett effect under resonant driving in a cavity magnomechanics system to induce n-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations, then relies on dissipative dynamics to generate bundle emissions.
result: Demonstrates that n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions can be generated and tuned by controlling system parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new method for generating nonclassical states in hybrid magnomechanical systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and sensing.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Separable Squeezed States In Finite-memory Structured Reservoir
authors: Austen Couvertier And Ting Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Austen Couvertier and Ting Yu

Entanglement in continuous-variable Gaussian systems is a key resource, and common reservoirs can both suppress and generate correlations. Existing work focused on preentangled states or Markovian baths, leaving open whether separable squeezed inputs entangle in structured environments or under modu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063724] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement generation from separable squeezed states in a finite-memory structured reservoir, extending previous work on Markovian baths.
motivation: Understanding how structured environments can generate entanglement from initially separable states is important for continuous-variable quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of two squeezed states coupled to a common non-Markovian reservoir with finite memory, using exact master equations.
result: They find that entanglement can be generated from separable squeezed inputs, and the non-Markovian memory enhances entanglement compared to Markovian reservoirs.
conclusion: Structured reservoirs can be exploited to create and control entanglement in continuous-variable systems, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Beyond Qubits: Multilevel Quantum Sensing For Dark Matter
authors: Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, And Ernst David Herbschleb
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, and Ernst David Herbschleb

Searching for ultralight dark matter requires detecting extremely weak oscillating fields, where quantum sensing is especially promising. The authors show that spin-1 nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond can harness multilevel quantum states to combine enhanced signal response with common mode noise suppression, improving sensitivity to axion-electron dark matter interactions.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060802] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: NV centers in diamond with multilevel quantum states enhance sensitivity for detecting ultralight dark matter.
motivation: Ultralight dark matter detection requires extremely sensitive quantum sensors; NV centers offer a promising platform.
method: The authors propose using spin-1 NV centers with multilevel quantum states to combine enhanced signal response with common-mode noise suppression.
result: The multilevel approach improves sensitivity to axion-electron dark matter interactions compared to conventional qubit-based sensing.
conclusion: Multilevel quantum sensing with NV centers is a viable and improved method for dark matter detection.

title: Coherent Perfect Absorption Of Anti-modes In An Indirect Coupled Magnon-polariton System
authors: Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, And Can-Ming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, and Can-Ming Hu

In this work, we report coherent perfect absorption (CPA) of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon–polariton system. By examining both single and indirectly coupled cases, we experimentally distinguish the modal decay rate [MATH] from the effective decay rate [MATH]. At CPA, ${γ}_{\m…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224431] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent perfect absorption of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon-polariton system, distinguishing modal and effective decay rates.
motivation: Understanding and controlling absorption in hybrid magnon-polariton systems is important for quantum information processing and signal manipulation.
method: The authors experimentally study single and indirectly coupled magnon-polariton systems, measuring decay rates and achieving coherent perfect absorption.
result: They successfully distinguish the modal decay rate from the effective decay rate and demonstrate CPA of anti-modes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into decay dynamics in hybrid systems and offers a method for achieving perfect absorption, relevant for quantum transducers and signal processing.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
authors: Gerardo Suárez And Michał Horodecki
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains accuracy while reducing complexity.
method: They express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the master equation to be solved more efficiently using standard techniques.
result: The approximation yields accurate dynamics for a range of non-Markovian regimes, significantly lowering computational cost compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This approach makes non-Markovian master equations more accessible for practical simulations, benefiting studies of open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize and estimate parameters of non-Markovian quantum dynamics in a collision model.
motivation: Characterizing non-Markovian dynamics is important for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often computationally expensive. QELMs offer a resource-efficient alternative.
method: The authors implement a QELM where the reservoir is a quantum system with memory, processing input states from a collision model to learn and estimate parameters of the dynamics.
result: The QELM successfully estimates parameters of the non-Markovian dynamics, demonstrating that memory-enhanced reservoirs improve learning performance compared to memoryless ones.
conclusion: Memory-enhanced QELMs are effective for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, providing a practical tool for quantum system identification.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations, relevant to the origins of life and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how simple molecular systems can extract energy from cyclic environmental changes without complex machinery, as a model for prebiotic energy harvesting.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a chemical system driven by a cyclic external field, analyzing energy extraction using stochastic thermodynamics and master equations.
result: They show that cyclic environments can power chemical reactions, with efficiency depending on the cycle frequency and system parameters, and identify conditions for net energy harvesting.
conclusion: Cyclic environmental fluctuations provide a robust physical mechanism for harvesting chemical power, which may have been crucial for the emergence of life.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables across both regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, with implications for non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and discusses how phase separation, multi-component condensates, and kinetic control can implement computations like sensing, classification, and memory.
result: It identifies specific features of phase transitions—such as thresholding, multistability, and temporal dynamics—that are analogous to computational primitives.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a plausible physical substrate for cellular information processing, suggesting new directions for synthetic biology and understanding of living systems.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower equilibration with nuclear spins.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs the heating dynamics, providing insights into thermalization in confined systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors apply EIT to achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of atom arrays in a finite magnetic field, leveraging the transparency and slow-light effects to reduce scattering and atom loss.
result: They demonstrate improved loading efficiency and imaging fidelity compared to standard techniques, enabling continuous operation of atom arrays.
conclusion: EIT-based loading and imaging is a practical method for enhancing neutral-atom array platforms, with potential applications in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle at intermediate frequencies.
method: The authors develop a technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling spectroscopy in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a semiconductor qubit platform, extracting noise cross-correlation spectra and revealing correlated noise sources.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction codes can be optimized.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, tailored to neutral-atom hardware constraints such as long-range interactions and native multi-qubit gates.
result: The architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit layout, space, and time overhead compared to conventional approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations with realistic hardware parameters.
conclusion: The transversal architecture provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, demonstrating the viability of neutral atoms for beyond-classical quantum computation.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper provides estimates of loss function concentration in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, linking noise resilience to circuit expressivity.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus and noise, hindering trainability; understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function gradient under noise, using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
result: They show that noise can mitigate barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to more concentrated loss functions that are easier to optimize.
conclusion: The results provide a principled link between noise and trainability, offering a roadmap for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and experimental demonstrations with trapped ions to probe string-breaking dynamics in different regimes.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics of confining strings, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They achieve suppression of leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical method to enhance qubit performance in exchange-only spin qubit platforms.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with practical quantum chemistry computations, improving reliability despite hardware noise.
method: Employs trapped-ion qubits with noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to perform a molecular energy calculation.
result: Achieves a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry on current hardware, paving the way for reliable quantum simulations.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical and analytical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor networks.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the connections between seemingly disparate approaches and offers a roadmap for future developments in non-Markovian open quantum system simulations.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qudits offer potential resource savings in quantum circuits, such as simplifying the Toffoli gate, but their role in quantum computing is not yet fully exploited.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can reduce the number of operations and qubits needed for certain multiqubit gates, and experimental demonstrations show feasibility in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, especially for reducing circuit depth and enabling algorithms on limited hardware.

title: Simulating Magic State Cultivation With Few Clifford Terms
authors: Kwok Ho Wan, Zhenghao Zhong, And Ainhoa Zapirain
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2134 (2026).

Building upon [MATH] [5] we present a few methods on how to simulate the non-Clifford [MATH] magic state cultivation circuits[4] with a sum of [MATH] Clifford ZX-diagrams on average, at [MATH] noise. Compared to a magic cat state stabiliser decomposition of all [MATH] non-Clifford spiders ([MATH] terms required), this is more than [MATH] times reduction in the number of terms. Our stabiliser decomposition has the advantage of representing the final non-Clifford state (in light of circuit errors) as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams. This will be useful in simulating the escape stage of magic state cultivation, where one needs to port the resultant state of cultivation into a larger Clifford circuit with many more qubits. Still, it's necessary to only track [MATH] Clifford terms. Our result sheds light on the simulability of operationally relevant, high [MATH]-count quantum circuits with some internal structure. Finally, we provide numerical results for full non-Clifford stabiliser rank simulation based on [MATH] along with optimisations using our cutting decompositions. Nearly [MATH] shots per second can be obtained on a laptop for the smaller [MATH] circuits at uniform circuit level noise [MATH], making it only [MATH][MATH] times slower than its (circuit-unspecific and un-optimised) fully Clifford proxy simulation via [MATH] using [MATH] gates.

.
tldr: This paper presents methods to simulate magic state cultivation circuits using a sum of few Clifford ZX-diagrams, achieving a significant reduction in the number of terms compared to standard stabiliser decompositions.
motivation: Magic state cultivation is a promising approach for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating the non-Clifford circuits involved is computationally expensive. Efficient simulation methods are needed to study the escape stage and integrate cultivation into larger Clifford circuits.
method: The authors build on prior work to decompose non-Clifford magic state cultivation circuits into a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams, exploiting internal structure to reduce the number of terms. They also provide optimizations for numerical simulation.
result: They achieve more than a 1000-fold reduction in the number of terms compared to a naive stabiliser decomposition, enabling nearly 1000 shots per second on a laptop for small circuits at uniform noise.
conclusion: The proposed stabiliser decomposition makes the simulation of magic state cultivation tractable and highlights the simulability of high T-count circuits with internal structure, which is useful for fault-tolerance research.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

.
tldr: Analyzes optimal probe states and measurement strategies for multiparameter estimation of SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries, identifying states that achieve Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation is crucial for quantum metrology, but the optimal resources and achievable precision for non-commuting parameters are not fully understood.
method: The authors consider two-bosonic-mode scenarios, analyze the scaling of precision with total particle number, and evaluate estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables restricted to first two moments of generators.
result: Eigenstates of J_z for SU(2) and twin-Fock states for SU(1,1) allow simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for all three parameters; with restricted measurements, twin-Fock states enable Heisenberg scaling for two parameters.
conclusion: The work identifies specific quantum states as resources for multiparameter estimation and extends intuition from single-parameter interferometry to the multiparameter setting.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theories is crucial for quantum simulation but requires many measurements; classical shadows offer a path to sample-efficient estimation.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: The protocols provide a blueprint for efficient measurement of gauge-invariant observables in more general lattice gauge theories.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions with simulation security in the plain model.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical. This work aims to design a protocol that is both secure and feasible for experimental implementation.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitments and one-way functions to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for error correction and resource estimation.
result: The proposed QOT protocol is more efficient than prior works and includes practical considerations for experimental realization, such as error correction.
conclusion: The protocol advances the state of the art in quantum oblivious transfer by combining security with practicality, paving the way for experimental demonstrations.

title: Hamiltonian And Double-bracket Flow Formulations Of Quantum Measurements
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Luis Pedro García-Pintos
abstract: We introduce a framework that unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket (DB) gradient flows. We do so by providing explicit expressions for stochastic Hamiltonians that produce state dynamics identical to those that happen during continuous quantum measurements. When such dynamical processes are integrated over sufficiently long time intervals, they yield the same results and statistics as during wavefunction collapse. That is, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained (stochastic) Hamiltonian dynamics. Alternatively, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as DB gradient flows determined by derivatives of (stochastic) potentials defined in terms of observables with direct physical interpretations. The gradient flows minimize the variance of the monitored observable. Our derivations hold for general monitoring described by non-Hermitian jump processes. We show that such reinterpretations of measurement dynamics facilitate the design of feedback processes. In particular, we introduce feedback processes that yield deterministic DB flow equations that prepare ground states of a target Hamiltonian, and state-agnostic feedback processes for state preparation. We apply the latter for entanglement stabilization of a two-qubit system considering a setup with imperfect measurements and feedback delay. We conclude by re-interpreting feedback processes as gradient flows with tilted fixed points.
tldr: Unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket gradient flows, showing wavefunction collapse as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or gradient flows.
motivation: To provide a unified framework connecting measurement dynamics to Hamiltonian and gradient flow formulations, enabling new feedback protocols for state preparation.
method: Derives stochastic Hamiltonians and double-bracket flows that reproduce continuous measurement dynamics, and introduces feedback processes based on these reinterpretations.
result: Wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or as double-bracket gradient flows minimizing observable variance; feedback processes can prepare ground states and stabilize entanglement.
conclusion: The framework offers new tools for designing feedback processes in quantum systems, with applications to state preparation and entanglement stabilization.

title: Quantum Deformations Of $\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{R}))$. Part I: Fidelity And Experimental Benchmarking
authors: V. Mariscal, J. J. Relancio, L. Santamar\'ia-Sanz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work explores the effects of both the standard quantum [MATH]-deformation and the non-standard [MATH]-deformation of the Hopf algebra [MATH] on multi-qubit systems. By constructing the states of a Hilbert space of [MATH] qubits through the Clebsch-Gordan coefficients associated with the deformed algebras, we show that these states naturally coincide with the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian of the [MATH]- and [MATH]-deformed Kittel-Shore models. We compare the resulting deformed states with those typically targeted in quantum information experiments, providing a bridge between algebraic constructions and experimentally relevant quantum resources. Fidelities with respect to the undeformed states are computed to establish how the quantum correlations are affected, both for few-qubit systems (including Dicke and non-Dicke states), and in the macroscopic limit ([MATH]) through closed-form formulas derived for arbitrary Dicke states. The results reveal different behaviors between the two deformations. The [MATH]-deformation smoothly modifies the states and maintains a residual overlap with the original configurations, while the [MATH]-deformation rapidly makes the states orthogonal to their undeformed counterparts. Both models demand a standard [MATH] rescaling to preserve fidelity stability in the macroscopic limit.
tldr: This paper studies quantum deformations of sl(2,R) and their effect on multi-qubit states, comparing fidelities with standard quantum information states.
motivation: To understand how quantum group deformations modify quantum correlations and to bridge algebraic constructions with experimentally relevant quantum resources.
method: Constructs multi-qubit states using deformed Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and computes fidelities with undeformed states for Dicke and non-Dicke states, including closed-form formulas in the macroscopic limit.
result: The standard q-deformation smoothly modifies states with residual overlap, while the non-standard h-deformation rapidly makes states orthogonal; both require rescaling to preserve fidelity in the macroscopic limit.
conclusion: Quantum deformations produce distinct modifications to multi-qubit states, with implications for quantum information experiments but no direct application to core quantum information theory.

title: Exact Operator Dynamics In Lindbladian Wess-Zumino-Witten Conformal Field Theories
authors: Qicheng Tang, Ruhanshi Barad, Xueda Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the time evolution of physical observables in open quantum many-body systems coupled to external environments is a natural and difficult problem, and exact results are still rare. In this work, we study this problem for Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) conformal field theories with Lindblad jump operators linear in Kac-Moody current modes. We investigate the exact operator dynamics generated by these Lindbladians, identifying classes of current operators whose Heisenberg equations close and can therefore be solved analytically using the underlying current algebra. In Abelian [MATH] WZW theories, this closure of operator dynamics holds for arbitrary settings of jump rates and includes exactly tractable cooling dynamics. In contrast, for non-Abelian WZW theories, exact closure occurs only for symmetric current-mode dissipation, where upward and downward current-mode transitions occur with equal rates, and even then it leads to a simple closed evolution only for a single current operator. Generic imbalances, including those needed for cooling, produce additional non-Abelian terms and prevent closure of the opeartor dynamics. Consequently, the current algebra gives rise to a broad family of exactly solvable dissipative dynamics in the Abelian setting, whereas in the non-Abelian case it singles out only a special exactly solvable dynamics corresponding to an infinite-temperature bath.
tldr: Exact operator dynamics in Lindbladian WZW CFTs are solved using current algebra, revealing closure for Abelian theories and a special symmetric case for non-Abelian theories.
motivation: Understanding time evolution in open quantum many-body systems is challenging; exact results are rare and valuable.
method: The authors study WZW CFTs with Lindblad jump operators linear in Kac-Moody current modes, using current algebra to identify classes of operators whose Heisenberg equations close.
result: In Abelian WZW theories, operator dynamics close for arbitrary jump rates, enabling exact cooling dynamics. In non-Abelian theories, closure only occurs for symmetric current-mode dissipation, yielding a single exactly solvable dynamics corresponding to an infinite-temperature bath.
conclusion: The current algebra provides a family of exactly solvable dissipative dynamics in Abelian settings, while non-Abelian theories are more restrictive.

title: Local Controllability Of Heralded Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Tommaso Francalanci, Nicol\`o Spagnolo, Mario Sigalotti, Eliott Z. Mamon, Ulysse Chabaud, Fabio Sciarrino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic linear optical networks provide a versatile platform for quantum information processing and quantum state engineering. However, the set of states that can be generated using passive linear optics alone is fundamentally constrained by bosonic symmetries. Heralding, based on conditional measurements on auxiliary modes, is a widely used technique to overcome these limitations and effectively enlarge the set of accessible states. Despite the widespread use of heralding, it is often unclear how specific ancillary resources impact the overall reachability of the target space. In this work, we investigate the local controllability of photonic states in linear optical networks by analyzing the rank of the Jacobian of the output state with respect to the underlying unitary circuit, which provides a quantitative measure of the dimension of the accessible tangent space at a given configuration. Our analysis ranges from passive linear optics to heralded linear optics, where auxiliary resources and conditional measurements are included. Within this framework, we quantify how different resources enlarge the locally accessible state space beyond that of passive linear optics and determine the resources required for the Jacobian rank to reach its maximal value, thereby achieving full local controllability. As maximal local rank is a necessary condition for global reachability, our framework offers a systematic tool to assess and compare the accessible state space of measurement-based photonic architectures, and to establish practical criteria for the resources needed in high-dimensional quantum state engineering.
tldr: This paper analyzes local controllability of photonic states in heralded linear optics using Jacobian rank, quantifying how ancillary resources expand the accessible state space.
motivation: Heralding in linear optics can overcome bosonic symmetry constraints, but the impact of specific ancillary resources on state reachability is unclear.
method: The authors compute the rank of the Jacobian of the output state with respect to the unitary circuit, providing a measure of the dimension of the accessible tangent space.
result: They quantify how different resources enlarge the locally accessible state space and determine conditions for achieving full local controllability.
conclusion: Maximal local rank is a necessary condition for global reachability, offering a systematic tool for assessing measurement-based photonic architectures.

title: Nearest-neighbour Gates Are All You Need: High-rate Quantum Low-density Parity-check Codes On A Planar Grid
authors: Boren Gu, Tamas Noszko, Vincent Steffan, Jens Niklas Eberhardt, Joschka Roffe, Jens Eisert, Stergios Koutsioumpas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-performance quantum low-density parity-check codes promise substantial reductions in the overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, but most constructions require long-range connectivity or qubit shuttling, both of which are difficult to realise in superconducting architectures. Here we introduce a family of quantum low-density parity-check codes that, for the first time, combines planar open-boundary layouts, finite-size advantages over surface codes, and syndrome extraction using only nearest-neighbour gates on a square grid of qubits. The key idea is to generate check-data connectivity dynamically: nearest-neighbour iSWAP walks both define the stabiliser supports and implement their measurement, avoiding the need for a long-range hardware graph. The resulting circuits achieve optimal constant-depth stabiliser measurement, independent of code size, and naturally remove leakage from the system by exchanging the role of check and data qubits at each syndrome extraction round. We find finite-size instances such as a [[323,14,15]] code, whose code-efficiency ratio is nearly an order of magnitude larger than that of rotated surface-code patches. At around 30 circuit qubits per logical qubit, the best directional tile-code layouts reduce the per-logical per-round logical error rate by up to a factor of 1000 relative to rotated surface-code memories. These results show that the advantages of quantum low-density parity-check codes can survive compilation into strictly planar nearest-neighbour circuits, bringing low-overhead fault-tolerant memories closer to near-term hardware.
tldr: Introduces a family of quantum LDPC codes that achieve high rates and finite-size advantages over surface codes using only nearest-neighbour gates on a planar grid.
motivation: High-performance quantum LDPC codes require long-range connectivity or qubit shuttling, which are difficult in superconducting architectures. The goal is to design codes compatible with planar nearest-neighbour hardware.
method: The authors use nearest-neighbour iSWAP walks to dynamically generate check-data connectivity, enabling constant-depth stabiliser measurement and leakage removal without long-range interactions.
result: They demonstrate a [[323,14,15]] code with nearly an order of magnitude larger code-efficiency ratio than rotated surface codes, and up to 1000x reduction in logical error rate per logical qubit per round.
conclusion: The work shows that advantages of quantum LDPC codes can be realized in strictly planar nearest-neighbour circuits, bringing low-overhead fault-tolerant memories closer to near-term hardware.

The codes also naturally handle leakage by swapping the roles of check and data qubits each round. The authors present finite-size instances, including a [[323,14,15]] code, and demonstrate that these codes achieve significantly higher code-efficiency ratios and lower logical error rates compared to rotated surface codes, with up to a factor of 1000 improvement in per-logical per-round logical error rate at around 30 circuit qubits per logical qubit.

limitations: The paper does not provide a full threshold analysis or compare against other QLDPC code families (e.g., hypergraph product codes) that may have better asymptotic scaling.

title: Entanglement Scaling And Problem Structure In Quantum Approximate And Adiabatic Optimization Algorithms
authors: Georgios Arapantonis, Paraj Titum, Gregory Quiroz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement is widely regarded as a key resource underlying the power of quantum algorithms and their potential to achieve quantum advantage. With the emergence of variational quantum algorithms, however, questions have arisen regarding how entanglement relates to problem structure and algorithmic performance in near-term quantum applications. Here, we examine this relationship through the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), a specific class of variational algorithms, applied to the MaxCut problem. We show that suboptimal variational parameter training can significantly modify the observed entanglement profile, obscuring its scaling behavior. By employing a high-performance optimizer, we find empirical evidence that QAOA exhibits entanglement scaling consistent with that of fermionic Gaussian states (up to a scaling factor) across a broad range of MaxCut instances. We further compare these results with adiabatic quantum computation, observing annealing-schedule-dependent entanglement profiles whose scaling behavior differs markedly from that of QAOA. Together, these findings provide new insight into how entanglement manifests in and distinguishes these two algorithmic paradigms, highlighting its connection to both computational performance and application structure.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement scaling in QAOA and adiabatic optimization for MaxCut, finding that QAOA entanglement resembles fermionic Gaussian states and differs from adiabatic annealing.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement relates to problem structure and performance in variational quantum algorithms is crucial for assessing their potential quantum advantage.
method: The authors apply QAOA and adiabatic quantum computation to MaxCut instances, using high-performance optimizers to avoid suboptimal parameter training, and compare entanglement scaling across algorithms.
result: QAOA exhibits entanglement scaling consistent with fermionic Gaussian states (up to a scaling factor), while adiabatic annealing shows schedule-dependent scaling that differs markedly from QAOA.
conclusion: Entanglement profiles distinguish QAOA from adiabatic optimization and are sensitive to training quality, highlighting the need for careful optimization in variational algorithms.

title: Electrical Noise Produced By Micron-Sized Particles Above A Surface Paul Trap
authors: Ben Saarel, Ozgur Sahin, Hartmut H\"affner, Alpha T. N'diaye
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric field noise produced by the surface of ion trap electrodes reduces the fidelity of quantum computing operations. Despite decades of investigation its microscopic origins remain unclear. Here, we measure electric field noise at trapping locations along the symmetry axis of a linear surface Paul trap. We find that noise levels vary by three orders-of-magnitude in one 600[MATH]m section of the trap. Optical and scanning electron microscope images show micron-sized particles close to the trapping locations with the highest noise levels. We find that modeling the particles as a lossy dielectric with a effective loss tangent [MATH] describes the magnitude of the noise, as well as its spatial and frequency dependence. Our observations may explain the large variation of reported noise levels in literature.
tldr: This paper investigates electric field noise from micron-sized particles on a surface Paul trap, attributing noise variations to lossy dielectric particles.
motivation: Electric field noise from ion trap surfaces limits quantum computing fidelity, and its microscopic origins are poorly understood.
method: Noise measurements along a linear surface Paul trap are combined with optical and SEM imaging to identify particles, and a lossy dielectric model is used to fit the noise magnitude, spatial, and frequency dependence.
result: Noise levels vary by three orders of magnitude in a 600 μm section, correlated with micron-sized particles; the lossy dielectric model with effective loss tangent describes the noise well.
conclusion: Micron-sized particles on trap surfaces are a likely source of the large variation in reported electric field noise, and modeling them as lossy dielectrics explains the observations.

title: Stalls And Spequlation: Pipelined Execution For Fault Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Aditi Awasthi, Gokul Subramanian Ravi, Jonathan Mark Baker
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires the coordinated action of three distinct systems: classical control logic, quantum hardware, and classical error decoders. Current scheduling models treat logical operations as atomic, hiding the fact that these subsystems operate sequentially and spend significant time idle. We present a pipelined execution framework that decomposes each logical operation into its component stages i.e. Control, Execute, and Decode. Building on this, we discuss some speculation strategies that allow successor operations to begin processing before their predecessors have completed decoding. We evaluate our framework on several common benchmarks and show that pipelining with speculation reduces total pipeline steps by 20-40% compared to a no-speculation baseline. The most aggressive strategy consistently outperforms conservative alternatives, even though partial rollback is needed at times, because the per-rollback penalty is small relative to the parallelism gained. We further show that speculation facilitates load balancing by distributing work more evenly across the heterogeneous subsystems of a fault-tolerant quantum computer, converting idle time into useful computation while also saving on execution time.
tldr: A pipelined execution framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation that decomposes logical operations into control, execute, and decode stages, using speculation to reduce idle time.
motivation: Current fault-tolerant quantum computing models treat logical operations as atomic, leading to idle subsystems and inefficiency. The authors aim to improve throughput by pipelining and speculation.
method: They propose a pipelined execution model where each logical operation is split into Control, Execute, and Decode stages, and introduce speculation strategies that allow successor operations to start before predecessors finish decoding.
result: Pipelining with speculation reduces total pipeline steps by 20-40% compared to a no-speculation baseline, with the most aggressive strategy consistently outperforming conservative ones despite occasional rollbacks.
conclusion: Speculative pipelining improves resource utilization and reduces execution time in fault-tolerant quantum computation, converting idle time into useful computation.
