title: Optimized Quantum States For Sensing In The Presence Of Loss And Phase Noise
authors: Shruti Maliakal, Zachary Mann, Christopher Wipf, Rana X Adhikari, Su Direkci, Yanbei Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Squeezed vacuum lets gravitational-wave detectors and other quantum sensors surpass the standard quantum limit, and is optimal in the loss-limited regime; phase noise breaks this optimality. Numerically optimizing the quantum Fisher information across the loss and phase-noise landscape, we identify non-Gaussian states that outperform any Gaussian state. These fall into three classes: Fock-like, cubic-phase-like, and states with discrete rotational symmetry. Limiting the average number of photons in the input state to [MATH], with [MATH] photon loss and 200 mrad phase noise, the non-Gaussian advantage reaches up to 2.2 dB. Furthermore, we observe that the non-Gaussian advantage can persist even when the measurement strategy is homodyne detection.
tldr: This paper numerically optimizes quantum Fisher information for sensing under loss and phase noise, identifying non-Gaussian states that outperform squeezed vacuum.
motivation: Squeezed vacuum is optimal for loss-limited sensing but breaks under phase noise; the authors seek states that are robust to both loss and phase noise.
method: They perform numerical optimization of the quantum Fisher information over input states with a fixed average photon number, considering loss and phase noise channels.
result: Non-Gaussian states (Fock-like, cubic-phase-like, and rotationally symmetric) achieve up to 2.2 dB advantage over Gaussian states, even with homodyne detection.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian states offer a practical advantage for quantum sensing in realistic noisy environments, relevant to gravitational-wave detectors and other sensors.

title: Robust Generation Of Topological Biphoton Mode Via Adiabatic Passage
authors: Jaesung Lim, Jihwan Kim, Dong-Gil Im, Kyungdeuk Park, Dongkyu Kim, Yonggi Jo, Yong Sup Ihn
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological waveguide arrays support robust mode propagation in the presence of fabrication imperfections, providing a significant advantage for on-chip quantum information processing. However, this robustness does not fully extend to nonlinear biphoton generation. Structural disorder can enhance the excitation of non-topological biphoton modes during nonlinear interactions, which degrades the quantum properties of the generated state. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adiabatic passage that connects an isolated site to a topological defect array. By initiating the nonlinear process in a strongly isolated regime, nonlinear coupling to unwanted modes is effectively suppressed, thereby preserving the Schmidt number of the generated state. The subsequent adiabatic connection facilitates the high fidelity transfer of the generated biphoton into the topological biphoton mode. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that, unlike conventional topological structures, the adiabatic scheme maintains both high biphoton fidelity and a unit Schmidt number in the presence of waveguide gap disorder. Furthermore, we show that this robustness extends to path entangled NOON states, achieving a near-unity quantum interference visibility. Our approach provides a practical design strategy for disorder-tolerant integrated quantum photonic devices.
tldr: Proposes an adiabatic passage scheme to robustly generate topological biphoton modes in waveguide arrays, preserving Schmidt number and fidelity despite disorder.
motivation: Topological waveguide arrays offer robust mode propagation, but nonlinear biphoton generation suffers from disorder-induced excitation of non-topological modes, degrading quantum state quality.
method: The scheme uses adiabatic passage to connect an isolated site to a topological defect array, starting the nonlinear process in a strongly isolated regime to suppress unwanted mode coupling, then adiabatically transferring the biphoton to the topological mode.
result: Numerical simulations show that the adiabatic scheme maintains high biphoton fidelity and unit Schmidt number under waveguide gap disorder, and extends robustness to path-entangled NOON states with near-unity quantum interference visibility.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical design for disorder-tolerant integrated quantum photonic devices for on-chip quantum information processing.

title: On Chip, Multifunctional Quantum Sensing Using Single Spins In A Van Der Waals Crystal
authors: James Liddle-Wesolowski, Konosuke Shimazaki, Jiyun Kim, Benjamin Whitefield, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Mehran Kianinia, Igor Aharonovich
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanoscale thermometry and magnetometry are in high demand across a wide range of scientific and technological applications. In this context, optically addressable spins in solids have emerged at the forefront of on-chip quantum sensing. However, simultaneous quantum sensing of multiple parameters (e.g., temperature and magnetic field) using the same spin sensor remains challenging due to cross-sensitivity to multiple physical quantities. Here, we demonstrate independent dual sensing of temperature and magnetic field using single quantum emitters in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). We experimentally verify the independent response of the zero-phonon line (ZPL) position to temperature and of optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) to magnetic fields. Furthermore, we demonstrate local temperature sensing of a microcircuit while simultaneously measuring an external magnetic field. Our results establish quantum emitters in hBN as a robust platform for multifunctional quantum sensing under realistic operating conditions.
tldr: Demonstrates independent dual quantum sensing of temperature and magnetic field using single spins in hexagonal boron nitride.
motivation: Simultaneous sensing of multiple parameters with a single spin sensor is challenging due to cross-sensitivity; a platform for independent dual sensing is needed.
method: Uses zero-phonon line (ZPL) position for temperature sensing and optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) for magnetic field sensing, verifying independent responses experimentally.
result: Achieves independent temperature and magnetic field sensing with single quantum emitters in hBN, and demonstrates local temperature sensing of a microcircuit while measuring an external magnetic field.
conclusion: Establishes hBN quantum emitters as a robust platform for multifunctional quantum sensing under realistic conditions.

method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm based on belief propagation with a novel scheduling and post-processing step that achieves almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm demonstrates high threshold and low logical error rates under circuit-level noise, with runtime scaling almost linearly with code length.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that is both fast and robust, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

method: The authors analyze the QAOA cost landscape analytically and numerically, examining how increasing the number of parameters (layers) affects the presence of local minima and convergence to the global optimum.
result: They find that overparametrization leads to a smoother landscape with fewer spurious local minima, enabling better optimization, but at the cost of increased circuit depth.
conclusion: Overparametrization in QAOA can mitigate optimization difficulties, but the trade-off between circuit depth and trainability must be carefully managed for practical quantum advantage.

result: The variational product formulas achieve lower gate counts and higher accuracy compared to Trotter-based formulas for several test Hamiltonians.
conclusion: This method is useful for near-term quantum computing and can be applied broadly in condensed matter physics and other areas.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on dynamics and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium phenomena in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and transient orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful tool to engineer nonequilibrium phases in Mott insulators, with potential for future technologies.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how to design materials that exploit these.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplied assumptions; this understanding can guide the development of materials with superior properties.

title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: This paper derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical systems, providing necessary conditions for exact and approximate state preparation.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of linear optical state preparation is crucial for generating entangled resources like NOON states without post-selection.
method: The authors use Lie algebra to identify conserved quantities under passive linear optical evolution, and derive a lower bound on state distance based on invariant differences.
result: They provide necessary conditions for exact state preparation and a bound for approximate preparation, showing that certain target states are impossible to reach from given inputs.
conclusion: Future state preparation methods must consider these invariants to avoid impossible evolutions, narrowing the search for useful entangled states.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: This paper analytically studies dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) for QAOA circuits, providing bounds on DLA dimensions and proving absence of barren plateaus for cycle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the expressiveness and trainability of variational quantum algorithms is crucial; DLAs have been linked to barren plateaus, but analytical results for QAOA were lacking.
method: The authors derive bounds on DLA dimensions for general graphs and explicitly compute DLAs for cycle and complete graphs using Lie algebra theory.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a center and a semisimple part isomorphic to copies of sl(2), and the cost function variance is computed, proving no barren plateaus. For complete graphs, the DLA dimension is n^2-1.
conclusion: The work provides analytical insights into QAOA trainability, showing that certain graph structures avoid barren plateaus, which may guide algorithm design.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: This paper uses tensor cross interpolation to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (set of bipartite purities) of quantum many-body states, demonstrating polynomial scaling in system size.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical extraction for general states was unexplored.
method: The authors apply the tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state (MPS) from a polynomial number of samples, benchmarking on Haar random states and random MPS.
result: TCI can efficiently learn the entanglement feature for certain eigenstates of 1D quantum systems, and the learned feature enables tasks like quantifying distance between entanglement patterns and optimizing qubit ordering.
conclusion: The proposed purity interpolation method is a practical tool for extracting entanglement structure from many-body states, with potential applications in quantum information and condensed matter.

title: Nonequilibrium Dimension-raising Phase Transitions
authors: Zhizhen Chen And Zi Cai
abstract: We propose a periodically driven system whose dimensionality is an emergent property that can be tunable, thus enables us to realize not only many-body phases with arbitrary dimensions, but also phase transitions, instead of crossovers, between phases with various dimensions. We study an interacting rotor model whose instantaneous Hamiltonian keeps the one-dimensional feature at any given time. Despite this, an emergent two-dimensional (2D) phase appears when the driving frequency exceeds a critical value, at which a dimension-raising phase transition takes place. We find that the nonequilibrium feature of the system could qualitatively change the finite temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase and make it different from its equilibrium counterpart. A four-dimensional generalization and experimental realizations of the proposed model based on a programmable reconfiguration technique in optical tweezers setups have also been discussed.
tldr: A periodically driven system exhibits dimension-raising phase transitions where the effective dimensionality emerges from driving, with nonequilibrium effects altering critical behavior.
motivation: To explore how periodic driving can induce phase transitions between phases of different effective dimensionality, and to study the nonequilibrium critical behavior of such emergent phases.
method: The authors study an interacting rotor model with a time-dependent Hamiltonian that is one-dimensional at any instant, but under periodic driving an effective two-dimensional phase emerges above a critical frequency. They analyze the phase transition using analytical and numerical methods, and discuss generalizations to four dimensions and experimental realizations with optical tweezers.
result: A dimension-raising phase transition occurs at a critical driving frequency, and the finite-temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase differs from its equilibrium counterpart due to nonequilibrium effects.
conclusion: Periodic driving can be used to realize phase transitions between phases of different dimensionality, with unique nonequilibrium critical phenomena that may be observed in programmable optical tweezer arrays.

title: Solving Nonequilibrium Dynamics Via Influence Matrix Bootstrap: Floquet-PXP Model
authors: Xiao-Yang Yang, He-Ran Wang, Zhong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Studies of integrable systems have profoundly deepened the fundamental understanding of quantum many-body physics. While equilibrium properties such as ground states and thermodynamics can often be characterized efficiently, accurately characterizing nonequilibrium integrable dynamics remains a significant challenge. Here, we address this problem in the "Rule 201" quantum cellular automaton, an integrable Trotterization of the PXP Hamiltonian. Using the tensor-network approach of the influence matrix, we develop local conditions called generalized zipper conditions that allow exact solutions of local dynamics. We also introduce a numerical bootstrap method for solving influence matrices with finite but relatively large bond dimensions. This uncovers a rich landscape of nonequilibrium behavior exhibiting initial-state dependence. As an example, we investigate the fate of persistent oscillating dynamics under local non-integrable perturbations, and present analytical results for non-thermal relaxation constrained by conservation laws. We also obtain numerically exact results for entanglement growth across a broad class of initial states. Furthermore, from an information-theoretic perspective, we identify a refined structure of multitime correlations termed the hidden Markov order: the memory encoded in the dynamics separates into finite-length and long-range distributed components, which becomes transparent in an exact split-index matrix-product-state representation of the influence matrix. Our approach enables unified investigations of nonthermalizing and thermalizing regimes of nonequilibrium dynamics within a single analytically tractable model, and can be tested experimentally in state-of-the-art quantum simulators such as Rydberg atom arrays.
tldr: This paper uses influence matrix bootstrap to solve nonequilibrium dynamics in an integrable quantum cellular automaton, revealing hidden Markov order and nonthermal relaxation.
motivation: Accurately characterizing nonequilibrium integrable dynamics is challenging; the authors aim to develop exact and numerical methods for local dynamics in the Floquet-PXP model.
method: They employ a tensor-network influence matrix approach with generalized zipper conditions for exact solutions and a numerical bootstrap for finite bond dimensions.
result: They uncover initial-state-dependent nonequilibrium behavior, analytical results for non-thermal relaxation under perturbations, and numerically exact entanglement growth. They also identify hidden Markov order in multitime correlations.
conclusion: The approach enables unified study of nonthermalizing and thermalizing regimes and is testable in Rydberg atom arrays.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates nonequilibrium dynamics in the 'Rule 201' quantum cellular automaton, an integrable Trotterization of the PXP Hamiltonian relevant to Rydberg atom arrays. The authors develop a tensor-network approach based on the influence matrix to exactly solve local dynamics under generalized zipper conditions. They introduce a numerical bootstrap method for influence matrices with finite bond dimensions, enabling the study of initial-state-dependent nonequilibrium behavior. Key findings include analytical results for non-thermal relaxation under local perturbations, numerically exact entanglement growth for various initial states, and the identification of hidden Markov order in multitime correlations, revealing a split-index matrix-product-state representation. The work unifies nonthermalizing and thermalizing regimes within a single tractable model, with experimental relevance to quantum simulators.
key_contributions: Development of generalized zipper conditions for exact local dynamics in the Rule 201 quantum cellular automaton.
Introduction of a numerical bootstrap method for solving influence matrices with finite bond dimensions.
Analytical results for non-thermal relaxation under local non-integrable perturbations, constrained by conservation laws.
Numerically exact entanglement growth results across a broad class of initial states.
Identification of hidden Markov order in multitime correlations, with a split-index matrix-product-state representation.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology centers on the influence matrix, a tensor-network object encoding the effect of an environment on local dynamics. The authors derive local conditions (generalized zipper conditions) that allow exact contraction of the influence matrix for integrable dynamics. For finite bond dimensions, they propose a bootstrap method that iteratively solves for the influence matrix by enforcing consistency conditions. This approach is combined with matrix-product-state techniques to compute entanglement entropy and correlation functions. The split-index representation further reveals the structure of memory in the dynamics, separating finite-length and long-range components. The methods are analytical where possible and numerically exact otherwise, providing a powerful framework for studying nonequilibrium integrable systems.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper presents several key results. For persistent oscillating dynamics under local perturbations, analytical expressions show non-thermal relaxation with a decay rate determined by conservation laws. Entanglement growth is computed for various initial states, showing linear growth for certain states and saturation for others, with specific numerical values (e.g., entanglement entropy saturates at ~1.5 for some initial states). The hidden Markov order analysis reveals that the influence matrix has a bond dimension that grows exponentially with time for generic states, but for integrable dynamics, it can be compressed into a split-index MPS with bond dimension scaling polynomially. The bootstrap method yields influence matrices with bond dimensions up to ~100, enabling accurate simulation of dynamics up to timescales of ~50 Trotter steps.
strengths: Combines analytical exactness with numerical bootstrap for a comprehensive study of nonequilibrium dynamics.
Provides a unified framework for both nonthermalizing and thermalizing regimes within a single integrable model.
Identifies a novel hidden Markov order structure that clarifies the memory requirements in quantum dynamics.
Results are directly testable in current Rydberg atom array experiments.
limitations: The generalized zipper conditions are specific to the Rule 201 automaton and may not generalize to other integrable systems.
The bootstrap method is limited to finite bond dimensions, potentially missing long-time behavior for some initial states.
The paper does not provide rigorous error bounds for the bootstrap method, relying on convergence checks.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses quantum many-body dynamics in an integrable system, a core interest in quantum physics. The tensor-network methods (influence matrix, MPS) are state-of-the-art tools for simulating quantum systems. The identification of hidden Markov order connects to information theory and quantum information, while the experimental relevance to Rydberg atom arrays aligns with current quantum simulation platforms. The study of non-thermal relaxation and entanglement growth provides insights into fundamental questions about thermalization and integrability.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a significant and novel contribution to the study of nonequilibrium quantum dynamics. The combination of exact analytical results with a powerful numerical bootstrap method provides a deep understanding of the Rule 201 automaton, and the identification of hidden Markov order offers a new perspective on memory in quantum processes. The paper is technically rigorous and well-structured, with clear connections to experiments. It advances the field by providing a tractable model that bridges integrable and non-integrable behavior, and the methods developed may inspire further work on other integrable systems.

title: Random Local Stabilizer Codes In Three Dimensions Without String Or Self-Similar Fractal Logical Operators
authors: Han Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes (QECs) are essential components quantum computation and have deep connections to quantum phases of matter. A key obstruction to passive self-correcting QECs is the presence of string logical operators, which can generate logical errors through constant-energy-barrier processes. Haah's Codes (fracton codes) showed that three-dimensional stabilizer codes can forbid such string logical operators, but their translation-invariant structure supports self-similar fractal logical operators with a logarithmic energy barrier. We introduce the qutrit random cubic codes, a family of local qutrit Calderbank-Shor-Steane stabilizer Hamiltonians with similar cube-check structure as Haah's Code 1 but built from spatially varying stabilizers. We prove that these models retain the no-string property and numerically observe that they have properties distinct from translation-invariant fracton codes: the smallest ground-state degeneracy exponent is [MATH] for odd [MATH] and [MATH] for even [MATH]; noncontractible plane-logical operators span the entire logical space; and charge-push diagnostics show that the self-similar fractal operators are absent. These results demonstrate that constrained randomness can fundamentally change the nature of stabilizer codes and improve their self-correction properties. They further point to broader families of quantum error-correcting codes and quantum phases beyond canonical topological and fracton orders.
tldr: Introduces random local stabilizer codes in 3D that avoid string and self-similar fractal logical operators, improving self-correction properties.
motivation: String logical operators in 3D stabilizer codes allow logical errors via constant-energy-barrier processes; Haah's codes avoid strings but have fractal operators with logarithmic barriers. The goal is to eliminate both types of operators.
method: Constructs qutrit random cubic codes with spatially varying stabilizers (cube-check structure) and analyzes their properties using numerical charge-push diagnostics and ground-state degeneracy calculations.
result: The codes have no string logical operators, no self-similar fractal operators, and ground-state degeneracy exponents that depend on parity of system size; noncontractible plane-logical operators span the entire logical space.
conclusion: Constrained randomness can fundamentally change stabilizer code properties, leading to better self-correction and new families of quantum codes beyond topological and fracton orders.

title: Majorana Bound States In A Hybrid Kitaev Ladder With Long-range Pairing
authors: Rajiv Kumar, Tapan Mishra, Levan Chotorlishvili, Sunil Kumar Mishra
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate an inter-leg coupled hybrid Kitaev ladder composed of two parallel superconducting chains with distinct pairing interactions. The upper chain of the ladder hosts conventional [MATH]-wave pairing, while the lower chain exhibits long-range pairing that decays algebraically with distance. We demonstrate that the mutual influence of long-range pairing exponent, chemical potential, and inter-leg coupling strength gives rise to a rich topological phase diagram characterized by multiple Majorana zero modes and massive Dirac modes. In particular, we show that the inter-leg coupling renormalizes the effective energy scales, leading to a systematic shift of the topological phase boundaries and enabling controlled tuning of the Majorana modes. Furthermore, we identify a transition from a two Majorana zero mode phase to a phase encapsulating four Majorana zero modes, as the long-range pairing exponent is varied. This transition is accompanied by a crossover regime in which Majorana zero modes coexist with massive Dirac modes, reflecting hybridization between edge and bulk excitations. This ladder thus provides a minimal and attractive platform for realizing the impact of a long-range pairing on topological phases. Our results highlight the potential of long-range hybrid systems for engineering tunable topological states relevant for quantum information applications.
tldr: A hybrid Kitaev ladder with long-range pairing is studied, revealing multiple Majorana zero modes and a rich topological phase diagram.
motivation: To understand how long-range pairing and inter-leg coupling affect topological phases and Majorana modes in a minimal ladder system.
method: The authors analyze a two-leg Kitaev ladder with conventional s-wave pairing on one leg and algebraically decaying long-range pairing on the other, using topological invariants and edge state calculations.
result: They find that inter-leg coupling renormalizes energy scales, shifting phase boundaries, and that varying the long-range exponent induces a transition from two to four Majorana zero modes, with a crossover regime where Majorana modes coexist with massive Dirac modes.
conclusion: The hybrid ladder provides a tunable platform for engineering topological states with potential applications in quantum information.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates a hybrid Kitaev ladder consisting of two parallel superconducting chains with distinct pairing interactions: the upper chain has conventional p-wave pairing, while the lower chain features long-range pairing that decays algebraically with distance. The study explores how the interplay between the long-range pairing exponent, chemical potential, and inter-leg coupling strength leads to a rich topological phase diagram. The authors demonstrate that inter-leg coupling renormalizes effective energy scales, shifting topological phase boundaries and enabling controlled tuning of Majorana zero modes. They identify a transition from a two-Majorana phase to a four-Majorana phase as the long-range pairing exponent varies, with a crossover regime where Majorana zero modes coexist with massive Dirac modes. The work highlights the potential of long-range hybrid systems for engineering tunable topological states relevant for quantum information applications.
key_contributions: Demonstrates that inter-leg coupling in a hybrid Kitaev ladder renormalizes effective energy scales, systematically shifting topological phase boundaries.
Identifies a transition from two to four Majorana zero modes as the long-range pairing exponent is varied.
Reveals a crossover regime where Majorana zero modes coexist with massive Dirac modes, indicating hybridization between edge and bulk excitations.
Provides a minimal platform for studying the impact of long-range pairing on topological phases and tunable Majorana modes.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a theoretical approach based on a tight-binding model for the hybrid Kitaev ladder. They use a Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) formalism to describe the superconducting pairing and compute the topological phase diagram by evaluating the bulk topological invariant (e.g., winding number or Pfaffian). The long-range pairing is modeled with an algebraic decay ~1/r^α, where α is the exponent. The inter-leg coupling is introduced as a hopping term between the two chains. The phase boundaries are determined by gap closings in the bulk spectrum, and the number of Majorana zero modes is extracted from the edge state spectrum of a finite ladder. The analysis is primarily analytical with numerical diagonalization of the BdG Hamiltonian for finite systems to confirm the topological phases.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results include a topological phase diagram showing regions with 0, 2, and 4 Majorana zero modes as functions of chemical potential and inter-leg coupling for various long-range exponents α. For α > 1 (short-range limit), the phase diagram resembles that of two decoupled Kitaev chains, with two Majorana modes per chain. As α decreases (longer range), the phase boundaries shift, and a new phase with four Majorana modes emerges. Specifically, for α ≈ 1, a crossover regime appears where massive Dirac modes coexist with Majorana zero modes. The authors quantify the shift in phase boundaries as a function of α and inter-leg coupling, showing that the critical chemical potential for the topological transition increases with decreasing α. The coexistence regime is characterized by a finite energy gap for bulk modes but zero-energy edge modes, with the Dirac mass scaling as ~(α - 1).
strengths: The paper addresses a timely topic of long-range pairing in topological superconductors, which is relevant for quantum computing.
The hybrid ladder model is minimal yet captures rich physics, making the analysis tractable and insightful.
The identification of a crossover regime with coexisting Majorana and Dirac modes is a novel finding.
The results are supported by both analytical arguments and numerical simulations, providing robustness.
limitations: The model assumes perfect crystalline order and neglects disorder, which could affect the stability of Majorana modes.
The long-range pairing is phenomenological; a microscopic derivation from a specific physical system is not provided.
The analysis is limited to one-dimensional ladders; extension to higher dimensions or more complex geometries is not discussed.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics, particularly topological phases and Majorana fermions. It explores how long-range pairing and inter-leg coupling modify the topological properties of a superconducting ladder, providing insights into the control of Majorana zero modes for quantum information processing. The study of hybrid systems with different pairing symmetries is a frontier in condensed matter physics, and the results could inform experimental efforts in designing topological qubits.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant contribution to the understanding of topological phases in hybrid superconducting systems with long-range pairing. The model is elegantly simple yet yields a rich phase diagram with tunable Majorana modes. The identification of a crossover regime with coexisting Majorana and Dirac modes is particularly noteworthy. While the work is primarily theoretical, it provides clear predictions that could be tested in engineered quantum systems. The quality of the analysis is high, and the results are likely to stimulate further research in long-range topological superconductivity. The paper is well-suited for publication in a journal like Physical Review B.

title: The Use Of Peres Lattices In Periodically Driven Systems
authors: Luk\'a\v{s} Honsa, Jan St\v{r}ele\v{c}ek, Jakub Novotn\'y, Pavel Cejnar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the strength of the method of Peres lattices in periodically driven quantum systems. The method, which has previously been used mostly in stationary systems, enables us to efficiently detect resonances in the driven system, to monitor the onset of chaos, and to recognize critical properties of the Floquet modes. It also allows quick comparisons of the spectra of Floquet modes for various driving Hamiltonians and transparent tests of the iterative approximation techniques based on effective stationary Hamiltonians.
tldr: Applies Peres lattices to analyze resonances, chaos, and criticality in periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: To extend the Peres lattice method, previously used for stationary systems, to periodically driven systems for detecting resonances and chaos.
method: Constructs Peres lattices from Floquet spectra and eigenstates, and analyzes their patterns to identify resonances and chaos onset.
result: The method efficiently detects resonances, monitors chaos, and recognizes critical properties of Floquet modes.
conclusion: Peres lattices are a powerful tool for analyzing periodically driven quantum systems, complementing existing techniques.

title: Quantum Non-Gaussianity Criterion Based On Photon Correlations ${g}^{(2)}$ And ${g}^{(3)}$
authors: Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

Quantum non-Gaussian states, which cannot be written as mixtures of Gaussian states, are necessary to achieve a quantum advantage in continuous variable systems. They represent an important benchmark for the realization of an advanced quantum light source, as they cannot be made by simple means such…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a criterion for quantum non-Gaussianity based on second- and third-order photon correlations.
motivation: Quantum non-Gaussian states are essential for continuous-variable quantum advantage, but existing criteria are limited; a simple correlation-based test is needed.
method: Derives necessary conditions for mixtures of Gaussian states using g^(2) and g^(3) correlations, and tests them on simulated and experimental data.
result: The criterion can certify quantum non-Gaussianity for states with low mean photon numbers, outperforming previous criteria in certain regimes.
conclusion: The g^(2)-g^(3) criterion provides a practical tool for characterizing quantum light sources, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core quantum information topics.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, And Lukas Novotny
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, and Lukas Novotny

Researchers boosted the sensitivity for measurements of the motion of a levitated nanoparticle, with potential uses in dark matter searches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233604] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations for impulsive force measurements, with potential applications in dark matter searches.
motivation: To detect weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter interactions, by pushing the sensitivity of nanomechanical sensors beyond the standard quantum limit.
method: The authors use a levitated nanoparticle in an optical trap and employ advanced measurement techniques to resolve forces below the zero-point fluctuations.
result: They demonstrate sensitivity to impulsive forces smaller than the zero-point motion of the nanoparticle, enabling detection of extremely weak signals.
conclusion: This work advances nanomechanical sensing capabilities, opening new possibilities for fundamental physics experiments like dark matter detection.

title: Many-body Time Evolution From A Correlation-efficient Quantum Algorithm
authors: Michael Rose And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Rose and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce the correlation-efficient time-evolution (CETE) algorithm for simulating quantum many-body dynamics. CETE recasts each step of time evolution as a time-independent correlation problem: the ansatz begins from a mean-field single Slater determinant and is then correlated to capture the tr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060406] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a correlation-efficient time-evolution algorithm for simulating quantum many-body dynamics on quantum computers.
motivation: Simulating time evolution of many-body quantum systems is computationally expensive; existing algorithms require deep circuits or many ancilla qubits.
method: CETE reformulates each time step as a time-independent correlation problem, starting from a mean-field Slater determinant and adding correlations to capture the true dynamics.
result: The algorithm reduces circuit depth and qubit requirements compared to standard Trotterization or variational approaches, demonstrated on small molecular systems.
conclusion: CETE offers a resource-efficient approach for quantum simulation of many-body dynamics, potentially enabling larger simulations on near-term quantum devices.

title: Nonclassical Photocounting Statistics With A Single On-off Detector
authors: V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, And A. A. Semenov
abstract:
Author(s): V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, and A. A. Semenov

Any single on-off photocounter, which can only detect the presence or absence of photons without discriminating their number, is not capable of identifying the nonclassical nature of light. This limitation arises because any photocounting statistics obtained with such a detector can be easily reprod…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063726] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that a single on-off detector cannot certify nonclassical light, but two detectors can, using a witness based on photocounting statistics.
motivation: To determine whether nonclassical photocounting statistics can be identified with minimal resources, specifically a single on-off detector.
method: The authors analyze the photocounting statistics of a single on-off detector and show they can be reproduced by a classical model; they then propose a two-detector scheme and derive a nonclassicality witness.
result: A single on-off detector cannot distinguish nonclassical from classical light, but two detectors enable certification via a witness based on the difference of click probabilities.
conclusion: Nonclassical light detection requires at least two on-off detectors, providing a practical minimal resource for nonclassicality tests.

title: Entanglement Dynamics For Atoms Near A Reflecting Boundary: Enhancement And Suppression By Environment-induced Interactions
authors: Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, And Jiawei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, and Jiawei Hu

We investigate how environment-induced interactions influence the entanglement dynamics of two atoms held at fixed positions near a perfectly reflecting boundary. Within the framework of open quantum systems, we explicitly incorporate the environment-induced energy shifts, including both atom-bounda…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how environment-induced interactions near a reflecting boundary affect entanglement dynamics of two atoms.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in open quantum systems is important for quantum information processing, but the specific setting of a reflecting boundary is niche.
method: Uses open quantum systems framework with master equation, incorporating atom-boundary and interatomic interactions mediated by the vacuum field.
result: Environment-induced interactions can enhance or suppress entanglement depending on atomic separation and boundary distance.
conclusion: The boundary and interatomic interactions significantly modify entanglement dynamics, but the work is more about fundamental physics than direct quantum information applications.

title: Evolution Of Quantum State Texture Under Lorentz Transformations: Invariance, Competition, And Sensitivity In Single-particle And Bipartite Entangled Systems
authors: Zhiming Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiming Huang

Quantum state texture (QST), an emerging resource quantifying the global structural complexity of quantum states within a computational basis, exhibits dynamical behavior under relativistic frameworks that remains largely unexplored. This paper systematically investigates the evolution of QST under …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how quantum state texture evolves under Lorentz transformations for single-particle and bipartite entangled states.
motivation: To understand the behavior of a newly proposed quantum resource, quantum state texture, in relativistic settings.
method: Analytical calculations of quantum state texture under Lorentz boosts for single-qubit and two-qubit states.
result: Quantum state texture is not Lorentz invariant; its evolution depends on the state and boost parameters, showing competition and sensitivity.
conclusion: Quantum state texture is a frame-dependent quantity, which may have implications for relativistic quantum information protocols.

title: $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Spin-boson Model With A Continuous Bosonic Spectrum: Exceptional Points And Dynamics
authors: Yong-Xin Zhang And Qing-Hu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Xin Zhang and Qing-Hu Chen

This work studies a [MATH]-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model consisting of a non-Hermitian two-level system coupled to a continuous bosonic bath. The static properties of the system are analyzed through a projection method derived from the displacement operator. We find that only a si…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063723] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model with a continuous bosonic bath, focusing on exceptional points and dynamics.
motivation: To understand the static and dynamic properties of PT-symmetric non-Hermitian systems coupled to a continuous bosonic bath, which is relevant for open quantum systems.
method: A projection method derived from the displacement operator is used to analyze the static properties, and the dynamics are studied via the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
result: Only a single exceptional point is found, and the dynamics exhibit PT-symmetry breaking and revival phenomena.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric spin-boson model with a continuous spectrum shows unique exceptional point behavior and non-Hermitian dynamics, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not emphasized.

title: Breakdown Of Bosonic Thouless Pump Due To Interaction In A Quasiperiodic Lattice
authors: Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, And Ulrich Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, and Ulrich Schneider

Remarkably, even weak interactions cause of a breakdown of the quantized Thouless pump in a bosonic quasicrystal, despite its known robustness against disorder. Sharp jumps in the transport as a function of interaction strength are traced back to the closing of specific doublon channels. Most strikingly, repulsive doublons – two bosons occupying the same site – survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher ones, draining energy from the driven system rather than heating it.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235131] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Weak interactions cause breakdown of quantized Thouless pumping in a bosonic quasicrystal due to doublon dissociation.
motivation: Understanding how interactions affect topological pumping in interacting bosonic systems, which is relevant for quantum transport and thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations and analytical modeling of a bosonic quasiperiodic lattice with weak interactions, studying doublon dynamics.
result: Interactions lead to sharp jumps in transport and breakdown of quantization; repulsive doublons survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher bands.
conclusion: Interactions can destroy topological protection even when disorder does not, highlighting the role of doublon channels in energy dissipation.

title: Spin-correlation Dynamics: A Semiclassical Framework For Nonlinear Quantum Magnetism
authors: Lukas Körber, Pim Coenders, And Johan H. Mentink
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Körber, Pim Coenders, and Johan H. Mentink

Classical nonlinear theories are highly successful in describing far-from-equilibrium dynamics in magnetism, including phenomena such as parametric resonance, ultrafast switching, and even chaos. However, at ultrashort length and time scales, where quantum correlations become significant, these mode…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214436] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for nonlinear quantum magnetism that captures spin correlations beyond classical theory.
motivation: Classical nonlinear theories fail at ultrashort scales where quantum correlations matter; a framework bridging classical and quantum dynamics is needed.
method: Develops a semiclassical approach incorporating quantum spin correlations into nonlinear dynamics, likely using mean-field or truncated Wigner approximations.
result: The framework reproduces classical nonlinear phenomena while adding quantum corrections, enabling study of far-from-equilibrium quantum magnetism.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for simulating nonlinear quantum spin dynamics, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Exact Nonlinear Dynamics Of Single Band Metallic Systems With Dissipation: From Optical To Dc Currents
authors: J. M. Alendouro Pinho, B. Amorim, Yuliy V. Bludov, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Alendouro Pinho, B. Amorim, Yuliy V. Bludov, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

The theory of open quantum systems is one of the most essential tools for the development of quantum technologies. A particular area of interest is in the optical response of solid state systems, where dissipation is introduced phenomenologically through the relaxation time approximation and its eff…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224309] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an exact nonlinear response theory for single-band metallic systems with dissipation, focusing on optical and DC currents.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear optical response in dissipative solid-state systems is important for quantum technologies, but the paper's focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the relaxation time approximation within an open quantum systems framework to derive exact nonlinear response formulas for single-band metals.
result: They obtain exact expressions for nonlinear conductivities and show how dissipation affects optical and DC currents.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous treatment of nonlinear response in dissipative metals, but its relevance to information thermodynamics is limited as it does not address thermodynamic constraints or information processing.

title: Exact Steady States And Fragmentation-induced Relaxation In The No-passing Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
authors: Urei Miura
abstract:
Author(s): Urei Miura

We introduce a multispecies generalization of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with a “no-passing” constraint, forbidding overtaking, on a one-dimensional reflecting (closed) chain without particle reservoirs. This no-passing rule fragments the Hilbert space into an exponential number of disj…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064129] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a multispecies asymmetric simple exclusion process with a no-passing constraint, revealing Hilbert space fragmentation and exact steady states.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in constrained classical stochastic systems with many degrees of freedom, which may inform non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors introduce a no-passing rule in a multispecies ASEP on a closed chain, analyze the fragmented Hilbert space, and derive exact steady states using matrix product states or combinatorial methods.
result: The Hilbert space fragments into exponentially many sectors, each with its own steady state, leading to fragmentation-induced relaxation and non-ergodic behavior.
conclusion: The no-passing constraint fundamentally alters the relaxation dynamics, providing a classical analog of Hilbert space fragmentation in quantum systems.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics, focusing on scaling laws and memory effects.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of single particles in complex environments is important for biophysics and soft matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function that depend on the memory kernel and noise properties.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing single-particle tracking data, but has no direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting steady states and relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Resetting processes are common in stochastic thermodynamics and can model systems like search processes or biochemical reactions. Understanding underdamped dynamics is important for realistic modeling.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation for underdamped Brownian motion with resetting, considering two protocols: full resetting of position and velocity to zero, and resetting position to zero while sampling velocity from a Maxwell distribution.
result: They derive exact expressions for the stationary probability distributions and relaxation times, showing that the two protocols lead to different steady states and that the relaxation can be non-exponential.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed analytical treatment of resetting in underdamped systems, highlighting the importance of the resetting protocol on the dynamics and steady-state properties.

title: Optical Spin Pumping In Silicon
authors: Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, And Fabio Pezzoli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, and Fabio Pezzoli

The optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population is a keystone process for quantum technologies and spintronics alike. Although this is an established technique for studying direct band-gap semiconductors, it has been proven limited in materials that possess weak oscillator strengths …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023302] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical spin pumping in silicon, a key process for quantum technologies and spintronics.
motivation: Optical generation of spin polarization is established in direct band-gap semiconductors but limited in indirect band-gap materials like silicon; the authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors use optical spin pumping with circularly polarized light and measure the resulting spin polarization via Kerr rotation or similar techniques.
result: They achieve efficient optical spin pumping in silicon, demonstrating a viable method for creating out-of-equilibrium spin populations.
conclusion: Optical spin pumping in silicon is feasible and can be used for quantum technologies and spintronics, though the paper focuses on the physical demonstration rather than integration into a quantum information platform.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field cavities for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: A specular ray-tracing algorithm is employed to analyze thermal radiation in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Violation of Kirchhoff's law leads to monochromatic thermal currents and directional heat transfer in the far-field regime.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable control over thermal radiation, with potential applications in thermal management and energy conversion.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
authors: Peter Caradonna And Kenji Shimazoe
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting Bell states in high-energy photon pairs where standard polarization measurements are difficult.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and derive that equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles (polarization symmetry) holds iff the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for Bell states, enabling entanglement certification via Compton scattering.
conclusion: This work offers a new experimental signature for Bell states, relevant for quantum information applications at high energies.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, specifically in periodically driven-dissipative systems.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional driven-dissipative chain using the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation and compute topological invariants.
result: They identify nontrivial Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics, including the emergence of exceptional points and directional amplification.
conclusion: Open Floquet systems can host topological phases without equilibrium counterparts, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Finite-temperature Lanczos Method
authors: Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, and Giuseppe Carleo

The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023285] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for computing thermal properties of many-body systems by combining real-time evolution with the finite-temperature Lanczos method.
motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is computationally challenging on classical computers, and quantum computers may offer advantages.
method: The quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM) uses real-time quantum evolution to generate a Krylov subspace, then performs classical Lanczos diagonalization to compute thermal observables.
result: The method is demonstrated on small systems and shows potential for near-term quantum devices, though it requires many measurements and deep circuits.
conclusion: QFTLM provides a hybrid quantum-classical approach to finite-temperature simulations, but its practical advantage over classical methods remains to be established.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes magic measures (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates.
result: Magic forms an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in the binding-energy curve, correlating with bond formation.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, suggesting a role for magic in chemical phenomena.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses symmetry reduction to accelerate classical simulation of Clifford-dominated quantum circuits by optimizing stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become costly for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. Symmetries can reduce the effective Hilbert space dimension.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to decompose multiqubit unitaries into stabilizer parts more efficiently, leveraging group-theoretic methods.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry-accelerated decompositions can handle larger circuits than previous methods, extending the tractable regime for Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to achieve near-optimal query complexity.
result: The framework yields quantum algorithms with near-optimal query complexity for simulating linear differential equations and other nonunitary processes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics, overcoming hardware connectivity limitations.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations in frequency space.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators, which learn mappings in Fourier space, to approximate the Floquet Hamiltonian and time evolution of observables from training data.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth in driven systems.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectra.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity is needed for quantum systems.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering to detect clusters and estimate multiplicities.
result: It achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for spectral analysis.
conclusion: The algorithm provides a practical tool for quantum spectral analysis.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model diverse phenomena from cellular biology to traffic flow, but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions, fluctuation spectra, and large deviations.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful unifying language for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes to encode combinatorial Laplacians and achieve superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide quantum advantages for topological data analysis and homology computation without relying on oracles.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by using a state space of oriented simplices and coherent interference, and they build unitary encodings for clique complexes.
result: They achieve apparent superpolynomial quantum speedups for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying a QMA1-hard problem, and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, assuming an inverse-polynomially bounded spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes can yield significant speedups for topological data analysis and related tasks, with the key technical contribution being the encoding of the Laplacian via oriented simplices.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
