motivation: Data assimilation for fluid dynamics is computationally expensive; modular approaches can reduce complexity while maintaining accuracy.
method: Combines second-order backward differentiation (BDF2) with a two-step nudging-based data assimilation scheme, making the analysis step explicit with implicit stability.
result: Stability and error estimates are proved, and numerical experiments show comparable accuracy to standard fully coupled assimilation with lower computational cost.
conclusion: The modular BDF2 assimilation method is an effective and efficient alternative for data assimilation in Navier-Stokes equations.

title: Counterexample To A Conjecture On The Pairwise Independent Correlation Gap Using Ai
authors: Karthik Natarajan Arjun Ramachandra
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aided by the AI tool GPT5.5 Pro, we provide a counterexample to a conjecture made by Ramachandra and Natarajan (2025) [Pairwise independent correlation gap, Operations Research Letters, 107255, 6040].
tldr: Using an AI tool, the authors provide a counterexample to a conjecture about the pairwise independent correlation gap.
motivation: To disprove a previously made conjecture in the field of correlation gaps.
method: The authors used the AI tool GPT5.5 Pro to construct a counterexample.
result: A counterexample to the conjecture was found.
conclusion: The conjecture is false, and AI tools can assist in mathematical discovery.

title: Twisted Quantum Loop Algebras Via Semi-derived Ringel-Hall Algebras
authors: Shiquan Ruan Ming Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted quantum loop algebras are a generalization of twisted quantum affine algebras in Drinfeld new presentation. The Hall algebras of Geigle--Lenzing's weighted projective lines are used to realize (untwisted) quantum loop algebras of simply-laced type associated to star-shaped graphs by Schiffmann and Dou--Jiang--Xiao. In this paper, we use the semi-derived Ringel-Hall algebras of more general weighted projective lines to realize the twisted quantum loop algebras associated to the valued star-shaped graphs, including the twisted quantum affine algebras in Drinfeld new presentation.
tldr: This paper uses semi-derived Ringel-Hall algebras of weighted projective lines to realize twisted quantum loop algebras, including twisted quantum affine algebras.
motivation: To generalize the realization of quantum loop algebras via Hall algebras to the twisted case, which is important for representation theory and mathematical physics.
method: The authors construct semi-derived Ringel-Hall algebras for more general weighted projective lines and show they realize twisted quantum loop algebras associated to valued star-shaped graphs.
result: They obtain a realization of twisted quantum loop algebras, including twisted quantum affine algebras in Drinfeld's new presentation.
conclusion: This work extends the algebraic framework for quantum loop algebras and provides a new perspective on their structure.

title: Geometric Realization Of Affine Bases: The Kronecker Quiver Case
authors: Jie Xiao Yumeng Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the transition matrix between the PBW basis and the canonical basis for the negative part of the quantized enveloping algebra of the Kronecker quiver from a geometric viewpoint. Building on Lusztig's geometric construction of the canonical basis, we construct sheaf-complex realizations of PBW basis elements by means of flag sheaf complexes over the strata [MATH] of representation varieties. Our first goal is to give a geometric description of the simple constituents appearing in the restrictions of these flag sheaf complexes to the strata [MATH]. This allows us to compare the PBW-type sheaf complexes with the simple perverse sheaves [MATH] arising in Lusztig's construction. Using this description together with a purity result for the relevant [MATH]-structures, we obtain another proof that the elements defined by Lusztig's perverse sheaves indeed form a basis of the composition algebra.Our second goal is to make the transition coefficients between the PBW basis and the canonical basis geometrically explicit. More precisely, we show that these coefficients are governed by the multiplicities of local systems in the restrictions of intersection cohomology complexes to smaller strata. As a consequence, the transition matrix from the canonical basis to the PBW basis is upper triangular with diagonal entries equal to [MATH], and its coefficients admit a direct geometric interpretation. In particular, in the Kronecker quiver case we recover the triangularity of the transition matrix and obtain positivity properties of the corresponding coefficient polynomials.
tldr: This paper studies the transition matrix between PBW and canonical bases for the quantized enveloping algebra of the Kronecker quiver using geometric methods.
motivation: To understand the relationship between two important bases in representation theory and to provide a geometric interpretation of the transition coefficients.
method: Uses Lusztig's geometric construction of canonical bases and constructs sheaf-complex realizations of PBW basis elements via flag sheaf complexes over representation varieties.
result: Shows that the transition matrix from canonical to PBW basis is upper triangular with diagonal entries 1, and coefficients have a direct geometric interpretation in terms of local system multiplicities.
conclusion: Provides a geometric proof of the triangularity and positivity properties of the transition matrix in the Kronecker quiver case.

title: Full Gabor Frames, Its Existence Problem, And A Non-uniform Balian-Low Type Theorem
authors: Rui Liu, Xin Ma, Yuxuan Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a broad class of Delone sets in [MATH] that are of significance in both mathematics and physics, we prove a non-uniform Balian-Low type theorem and settle the converse problem on the existence of Gabor frames, for arbitrary dimension [MATH]. To this end, we introduce a class of Gabor frames, termed full Gabor frames, and prove that the existence of such a frame on the Delone set with Schwartz window functions is equivalent to the condition that the lower Beurling density be strictly greater than one. In fact, the usual Balian-Low direction using window functions from the Feichtinger's algebra can be proven for arbitrary point sets, thereby improving an earlier density theorem by Christensen, Deng, and Heil. The corresponding dual result for Riesz sequences is also obtained. The main technical tools employed in this paper are tiling groupoid constructions and [MATH]-algebraic methods. As a byproduct, we resolve an open question from Ito's thesis concerning the bounded dynamical asymptotic dimension of tiling groupoids. Furthermore, this result allows us to extend the classification theorem of Ito, Whittaker, and Zacharias to the twisted case.
tldr: This paper proves a non-uniform Balian-Low type theorem and settles the existence problem of Gabor frames for Delone sets using tiling groupoid and C*-algebra methods.
motivation: The existence of Gabor frames on irregular point sets is a fundamental question in time-frequency analysis with applications in signal processing and physics.
method: The authors introduce full Gabor frames and use tiling groupoid constructions and C*-algebraic methods to characterize their existence in terms of Beurling density.
result: They prove that a full Gabor frame with Schwartz window exists on a Delone set iff the lower Beurling density > 1, and also resolve an open question on bounded dynamical asymptotic dimension of tiling groupoids.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of Gabor frame existence for a broad class of point sets and extends classification results to twisted groupoids.

title: Fourier Phase Retrieval For Finite Unions Of Intervals
authors: Zhiqiang Xu Yu Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the one-dimensional Fourier phase retrieval problem for indicator functions of finite unions of intervals. Specifically, we study the recovery of a set [MATH] from the magnitude of its Fourier transform [MATH], where each [MATH] is a bounded interval. For [MATH], we prove that [MATH] is uniquely determined by [MATH] up to the natural ambiguities of translation and reflection, and we further establish a stability result for this reconstruction. In contrast, for [MATH], uniqueness fails in general. More precisely, for every [MATH], we explicitly construct functions [MATH] such that [MATH] while [MATH] cannot be obtained from [MATH] by any translation or reflection, where [MATH] denotes the class of indicator functions of unions of exactly [MATH] intervals. Furthermore, building on the theory of the turnpike problem, in which a finite integer set is uniquely determined by its multiset of pairwise differences under a collision-free condition, we establish an analogous result for finite subsets of [MATH]. This, in turn, yields a sufficient condition for recovering indicator functions of finite unions of intervals. These results provide a complete characterization of the Fourier phase retrieval problem for indicator functions of finite unions of intervals and offer new insights into Fourier phase retrieval for indicator functions of more general domains in higher dimensions.
tldr: This paper studies the one-dimensional Fourier phase retrieval problem for indicator functions of finite unions of intervals, establishing uniqueness and stability results for two intervals and counterexamples for three or more.
motivation: Fourier phase retrieval is a classical inverse problem with applications in imaging and crystallography, but the specific case of indicator functions of unions of intervals has not been fully characterized.
method: The authors use analytic and combinatorial arguments, including the theory of the turnpike problem, to analyze uniqueness and construct counterexamples.
result: For two intervals, the indicator function is uniquely determined up to translation and reflection, with a stability result. For three or more intervals, uniqueness fails in general.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete characterization of the Fourier phase retrieval problem for this class of functions, offering insights for higher-dimensional generalizations.

title: Structure-Oriented Randomized Neural Networks For Poisson-Nernst-Planck And Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes Systems
authors: Fei Wang Yunlong Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a structure-oriented randomized neural network framework, termed SO-RaNN, for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck (PNP) system and the Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes (PNP-NS) system. The decoupled linearized subproblems are solved iteratively by randomized neural networks in a space-time framework. For the concentration variables, a pointwise cut-off is used to enforce positivity at the value level, and discrete mass-scaling factors are computed at selected correction instants and interpolated in time, so as to ensure exact mass matching at those instants and to promote approximate mass preservation between them. To introduce an auxiliary discrete dissipation mechanism, we further employ an SAV-type post-processing correction, which yields monotonicity of the SAV auxiliary variable under the ideal SAV update. For the PNP-NS system, a structure-preserving randomized neural network (SP-RaNN) is used for the velocity field, so that the velocity approximation satisfies the incompressibility constraint pointwise by construction. On the theoretical side, we derive residual-based estimates for the raw, uncorrected RaNN solvers of the linearized subproblems, formulate a conditional local-in-time convergence result for the raw outer Picard iteration of the PNP system, and analyze the value-level positivity correction together with the mass-correction and SAV post-processing steps. For the PNP-NS system, we establish an approximation result for the SP-RaNN space and provide a conditional error statement for the corresponding linearized Oseen-type problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate approximation accuracy in the source-driven manufactured tests and illustrate the intended value-level positivity correction, selected-time mass matching, computed free-energy curves based on the final gauge-fixed potential, and divergence-free approximation in benchmark tests.
tldr: This paper develops a structure-oriented randomized neural network framework for solving Poisson-Nernst-Planck and Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes systems.
motivation: To efficiently solve coupled nonlinear PDE systems arising in electrokinetics and fluid dynamics using neural networks while preserving physical constraints like positivity and incompressibility.
method: The authors propose a decoupled iterative scheme using randomized neural networks with pointwise cut-off for positivity, mass-scaling correction, SAV post-processing, and a structure-preserving network for divergence-free velocity.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate accuracy, positivity enforcement, mass conservation, and divergence-free approximation in benchmark tests.
conclusion: The SO-RaNN and SP-RaNN frameworks provide effective mesh-free solvers for PNP and PNP-NS systems with theoretical guarantees.

title: Two Examples Of Combinatorial Relations Among Relations Of $C_{n}\sp{(1)}$-standard Modules For Higher Levels
authors: Tomislav \v{s}iki\' C
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The construction of relations among relations is one ingredient in the Groebner-like basis construction of the maximal ideal of the universal vertex operator algebra [MATH] for affine Lie algebras. For affine Lie algebras of type [MATH], such combinatorially parametrized relations among relations were constructed in earlier work for level [MATH] standard modules , and for [MATH]-standard modules at higher levels . This article presents two further examples in which the same counting method can be carried out. The first treats [MATH]-standard modules at the fixed level [MATH], with [MATH] arbitrary. The second treats [MATH]-standard modules for arbitrary level [MATH]. In both cases the calculation compares the number of required relations among relations in a trapezoid of the array of negative root vectors with the corresponding representation-theoretic dimension.
tldr: This paper presents combinatorial relations among relations for standard modules of affine Lie algebras of type C_n^{(1)} at higher levels, extending previous work on Gröbner-like bases for vertex operator algebras.
motivation: The construction of relations among relations is a key step in building a Gröbner-like basis for the maximal ideal of the universal vertex operator algebra associated to affine Lie algebras, which is important for representation theory.
method: The authors use combinatorial counting methods to compare the number of required relations among relations in a trapezoid of negative root vectors with the corresponding representation-theoretic dimension, providing two examples: one for level 2 standard modules with arbitrary n, and one for arbitrary level with n=2.
result: The counting method successfully yields the required number of relations among relations in both examples, matching the representation-theoretic dimension.
conclusion: The examples demonstrate the applicability of the combinatorial counting method to higher-level standard modules, suggesting potential for further generalization.

title: Optimization With Inequality Constraints By The Embedded Gradient Vector Field Method
authors: Petre Birtea, Ioan Casu, Dan Comanescu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric framework for constrained optimization problems with inequality constraints through the introduction of quadratic slack variables. This formulation makes it possible to employ the language of Riemannian geometry and to solve the problem via the embedded gradient vector field method. We lift the feasible set to a smooth submanifold of an extended ambient space. The stratified structure of the resulting constraint manifold is analyzed in detail, yielding a natural partition according to which constraints are active. Using the embedded gradient vector field formalism, we derive explicit, determinantal formulas for the Lagrange multiplier functions directly from the geometry of the constraint manifold, recovering and re-framing the classical Karush-Kuhn-Tucker first-order necessary conditions without invoking the classical Lagrange multiplier method. Second-order optimality conditions are obtained by computing the restricted Hessian on each stratum, and a complete sign condition on the Lagrange multipliers is identified as the geometric counterpart of the classical complementary slackness condition. The theory is illustrated on the double ice-cream cone example, where the geometry of the problem determines the nature and number of local minima.
tldr: A geometric framework for constrained optimization with inequality constraints using quadratic slack variables and embedded gradient vector fields.
motivation: To provide a geometric perspective on constrained optimization that recasts KKT conditions and complementary slackness in terms of Riemannian geometry.
method: Introduces quadratic slack variables to transform inequality constraints into equality constraints on a smooth submanifold, then applies embedded gradient vector field dynamics to find optima.
result: Derives explicit formulas for Lagrange multipliers, second-order optimality conditions via restricted Hessian, and a geometric interpretation of complementary slackness.
conclusion: The geometric approach offers an alternative viewpoint on classical optimization theory, illustrated on the double ice-cream cone example.

title: Vancomycert: A Certified Neuro-Symbolic Drug Delivery System (Case Study)
authors: Alistair Sirman, Fleur Conway, Jessica Ciupa, Gusts Gustavs Gr\=inbergs, Ekaterina Komendantskaya, Thai Son Hoang, Michael Rawson, Alessandro Bruni, Vaishak Belle, Michael John Williams
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural network controllers for autonomous decision-making are well-established in cyber-physical systems, yet their deployment in safety-critical healthcare settings remains largely unverified. This paper presents a methodology and case study for the formal verification of a neural network controller for antibiotic dosing, motivated by the challenge of systems that must be simultaneously adaptive and provably safe across unbounded time horizons. We construct a simplified yet clinically-interpretable model that tracks drug concentration, body temperature, and white blood cell count. Vancomycin is selected as a representative antibiotic, widely prescribed for severe infections yet carrying a narrow therapeutic window, where supratherapeutic concentrations risk nephrotoxicity and subtherapeutic dosing risks treatment failure. A supervised neural network controller is trained on synthetic clinician-style dosing data. We establish formal verification of input-output safety properties, specifically verifying a property of a neural network that implies an infinite-horizon proof that automated dosing never exceeds the supratherapeutic boundary. This system property is proven in Rocq using the Vehicle interactive theorem prover back-end to integrate the different proof systems. The end result is a verification pipeline that allows for a wide variety of treatment approaches whilst maintaining safety for each specific patient.
tldr: This paper presents a formal verification pipeline for a neural network controller for antibiotic dosing, ensuring safety over infinite time horizons.
motivation: Neural network controllers in healthcare require formal safety guarantees, especially for drugs with narrow therapeutic windows like vancomycin.
method: A simplified clinical model tracks drug concentration, temperature, and white blood cell count; a supervised neural network is trained on synthetic dosing data, and safety properties are verified using the Vehicle interactive theorem prover in Rocq.
result: The verification proves that automated dosing never exceeds the supratherapeutic boundary over an infinite horizon.
conclusion: The methodology demonstrates a viable pipeline for certifying neural network controllers in safety-critical medical applications.

title: G-Lox: Group-Adaptive, Privacy-Preserving Bridge Distribution With Two-Party Computation
authors: Nicholas Hopper Baigang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present G-Lox (group-adaptive Lox), a bridge-distribution system that preserves Lox-style distributor blindness while enabling hidden, stateful group-level adaptation. G-Lox places adaptive assignment logic behind a two-server privacy wall, so no single server learns group identifiers or group-to-bridge assignments. Private state access and state-dependent updates use two-server DPF/FSS protocols and secure two-party computation, supporting blockage reporting, transport-aware reassignment, and privacy-preserving group splitting. We evaluate G-Lox through system measurements and policy simulation. In our C++/EMP implementation over real TCP sockets, private state access has low client-visible overhead: across state sizes up to 2^16, communication remains in the low-KiB range per iteration. At M=1024, the client sends 1,968 bytes, receives 1,280 bytes, and completes an iteration in about 0.25 s. Simulations with group-specific blocking and Sybil enumeration show that G-Lox improves robustness over Lox- and rBridge-like baselines among systems that maintain broad issuance.
tldr: G-Lox is a privacy-preserving bridge distribution system using two-party computation for group-adaptive assignment.
motivation: Existing bridge distribution systems lack privacy-preserving group-level adaptation, making them vulnerable to blocking and Sybil attacks.
method: The system uses two-server DPF/FSS protocols and secure two-party computation to hide group identifiers and assignments, with private state access and updates.
result: Implementation shows low client-visible overhead: communication in low-KiB range and iteration time ~0.25s for M=1024; simulations show improved robustness against blocking and Sybil enumeration.
conclusion: G-Lox demonstrates that group-adaptive, privacy-preserving bridge distribution is feasible with acceptable performance.

title: Low-Cost Multi-Precision Systolic Arrays For Accelerating Fhe NTTs On Ai ASICs
authors: George Alexakis, Dimitrios Schoinianakis, Giorgos Dimitrakopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) ensures robust data privacy but suffers from prohibitive computational overhead. Accelerating FHE on AI hardware like Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) is promising, yet fundamentally limited by a precision mismatch: TPUs are optimized for 8-bit arithmetic, whereas FHE and its critical parts such as the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), demand high precision. Current approaches bridge this gap using matrix decomposition to execute NTT computations on low-precision matrix engines. However, reconstructing the full-precision results requires shift-and-add accumulation that does not match the dataflow of matrix multiplication. This forces offloading full-precision reconstruction from matrix engines to vector processors that disrupts the matrix multiplication dataflow, creating significant performance bottleneck. To resolve this limitation, we propose a minimally modified multi-precision systolic array that performs full-precision output reconstruction natively within the array in sync with low-precision matrix multiplication under a uniform dataflow. Synthesized at 7nm with OpenRoad, our design incurs negligible hardware overhead. Cycle-accurate simulations using SCALE-Sim demonstrate that natively executing NTTs on the proposed architecture achieves at least 1.33x speedup, for transform sizes 2^12 to 2^16 on 128x128 matrix engines, successfully enabling standard AI hardware to support high-precision FHE acceleration.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-precision systolic array architecture to accelerate Number Theoretic Transforms for Fully Homomorphic Encryption on AI ASICs.
motivation: FHE acceleration on AI hardware is limited by precision mismatch between low-precision matrix engines and high-precision FHE computations.
method: The authors design a minimally modified systolic array that performs full-precision output reconstruction natively within the array, maintaining a uniform dataflow.
result: Cycle-accurate simulations show at least 1.33x speedup for NTTs on 128x128 matrix engines with negligible hardware overhead.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enables standard AI hardware to support high-precision FHE acceleration efficiently.

title: A Novel FeFET Differential Bit-Cell With Hybrid Volatile And Non-Volatile Memory Modes
authors: Jianze Wang, Wei Zhang, Xuanyao Fong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-volatile SRAM (nvSRAM) designs have been investigated to address the high leakage power of CMOS-based SRAM and the large write latency of emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) technologies. However, prior nvSRAM designs that combine SRAM with eNVM devices typically require backup and restore (B\&R) operations and incur significant cell-area overhead. Here, we propose a differential memory bit-cell consisting of a pair of cross-coupled ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) and a pair of access transistors, resulting in a four-transistor (4T) structure, which is smaller than conventional 6T SRAM and many prior nvSRAM designs. The proposed bit-cell can be configured to operate in either volatile or non-volatile mode by adjusting the write conditions. In the non-volatile mode, the proposed nvSRAM achieves a store power of 0.13~[MATH]W with a 2~ns store time, and no explicit B\&R operation is required. The proposed bit-cell can also be viewed as a cross-coupled gain cell, enabling further applications.
tldr: This paper proposes a compact 4T FeFET-based bit-cell that can operate in both volatile and non-volatile modes, aiming to reduce leakage power and cell area compared to conventional SRAM and nvSRAM designs.
motivation: CMOS-based SRAM suffers from high leakage power, while emerging non-volatile memories have large write latency. Prior nvSRAM designs combining SRAM with eNVM require backup/restore operations and incur significant area overhead.
method: The authors design a differential bit-cell using two cross-coupled ferroelectric FETs and two access transistors (4T structure). The cell can be configured to volatile or non-volatile mode by adjusting write conditions, and no explicit backup/restore is needed.
result: The proposed 4T nvSRAM achieves a store power of 0.13 µW with a 2 ns store time, and the cell area is smaller than conventional 6T SRAM and many prior nvSRAM designs.
conclusion: The FeFET-based bit-cell offers a compact, low-power hybrid memory solution that eliminates the need for backup/restore operations, making it suitable for applications requiring both volatile and non-volatile storage.

title: Spatially Robust Near-Field Swipt Using Pinching Antennas: Rate-Energy Tradeoff Bounds
authors: Zoran Hadzi-Velkov, Marija Poposka, Slavche Pejoski, Arumugam Nallanathan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching Waveguide Antennas (PWAs) offer significant potential for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) by enabling precise near-field energy focusing. However, existing optimization frameworks are largely point-based (targeting a single coordinate for maximum gain), and thus highly sensitive to positioning errors and mobility, as near-field signals fluctuate significantly even over small spatial displacements. In this paper, we propose a spatially robust design framework based on discrete antenna selection optimized for service area (SA) coverage. Unlike point-based approaches, our model guarantees quality of service within predefined SAs for both information decoding (ID) and energy harvesting (EH) receivers, thereby improving robustness to user displacements. We formulate the problem as a non-convex binary quadratic program aimed at maximizing harvested energy within the EH SA subject to robust rate constraints in the ID SA. To characterize fundamental performance limits, we develop a semidefinite relaxation (SDR) framework that provides an upper bound on the achievable rate-energy (R-E) region. For the lower bound, we employ a low-complexity swap-based local search algorithm enforcing binary hardware constraints. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed coverage-oriented design yields a robust R-E tradeoff and maintains stable performance across service regions, highlighting the advantages of discrete antenna activation over point-based near-field optimization approaches.
tldr: This paper proposes a spatially robust design for near-field SWIPT using pinching antennas, focusing on rate-energy tradeoff bounds.
motivation: Existing point-based near-field optimization for SWIPT is highly sensitive to positioning errors and mobility, motivating a coverage-oriented design.
method: The authors formulate a non-convex binary quadratic program for antenna selection to maximize harvested energy under rate constraints, and use semidefinite relaxation for upper bounds and a swap-based local search for lower bounds.
result: The coverage-oriented design yields a robust rate-energy tradeoff and stable performance across service regions, outperforming point-based approaches.
conclusion: Discrete antenna activation provides robustness to user displacements in near-field SWIPT systems.

title: Quantization As A Malicious Task: Removing Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors Via Task Arithmetic
authors: Kaihsun Yang, Min-Yan Tsai, Chia-Mu Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model quantization is widely adopted to reduce memory usage and inference cost when deploying deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices. However, recent studies have revealed a new security threat known as Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors (QCBs), where a model behaves normally in full precision but activates malicious behavior only after quantization. Existing defenses typically modify quantization procedures or correct activation statistics, often introducing additional computational overhead or relying on specific quantization settings. Here, we present QVec, a parameter-space perspective for defending against QCBs. We observe that the weight difference between a full-precision model and its quantized counterpart encodes a structured behavioral shift, which can be interpreted as a malicious task vector rather than random quantization noise. Based on this insight, QVec counteracts this malicious direction through controlled parameter correction prior to deployment. QVec requires no retraining, no trigger samples, and only a single quantization pass to estimate the parameter shift, together with a lightweight hyperparameter search. Extensive experiments across image classification benchmarks and multiple Large Language Model (LLM) attack scenarios demonstrate that QVec consistently suppresses backdoor activation while preserving clean performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a defense against quantization-conditioned backdoors in deep neural networks using task arithmetic.
motivation: Quantization-conditioned backdoors (QCBs) pose a security threat where models behave maliciously only after quantization, and existing defenses are costly or restrictive.
method: QVec interprets the weight difference between full-precision and quantized models as a malicious task vector and counteracts it via controlled parameter correction before deployment.
result: Experiments on image classification and LLM attack scenarios show that QVec suppresses backdoor activation while preserving clean performance.
conclusion: QVec provides an efficient, retraining-free defense against QCBs that requires only a single quantization pass and lightweight hyperparameter search.

title: Analyzing Defensive Misdirection Against Model-Guided Automated Attacks On Agentic Ai Systems
authors: Vivek Namsani Reza Soosahabi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly rely on language-model components to interpret instructions, process external data, invoke tools, and coordinate with other agents. These capabilities make prompt-injection and jailbreak attacks more consequential, especially as attackers adopt model-guided automation to scale probing, prompt refinement, and response evaluation. This work analyzes the resulting attack-defense setting through a probabilistic model of a target system, its defense mechanism, and the attacker's automated judge. Our analysis shows that conventional detect-and-block defenses can allow attacker success rate (ASR) to approach one as the query budget grows, since predictable refusals provide useful feedback to automated search. We then examine detect-and-misdirect, where detected malicious interactions receive controlled, non-operational responses designed to induce false-positive errors in the attacker's judge. This strategy reduces the positive predictive value of attacker-selected candidates and yields a bounded asymptotic ASR. We evaluate a proof-of-concept realization of this strategy through Contextual Misdirection via Progressive Engagement (CMPE), a lightweight conversational misdirection method designed to replace predictable refusal text with safe but strategically misleading responses in automated jailbreak settings. On jailbreak benchmarks, CMPE reduces estimated ASR upper bounds by up to two orders of magnitude and nearly eliminates verified attack success in end-to-end PAIR and GPTFuzz attack runs.
tldr: This paper analyzes defensive misdirection strategies against model-guided automated attacks on agentic AI systems, focusing on prompt injection and jailbreak attacks.
motivation: Agentic AI systems are vulnerable to prompt injection and jailbreak attacks, especially when attackers use automated model-guided tools to scale probing and refinement.
method: The authors model the attack-defense setting probabilistically, compare detect-and-block vs. detect-and-misdirect defenses, and propose Contextual Misdirection via Progressive Engagement (CMPE) as a proof-of-concept.
result: Detect-and-block allows attacker success rate to approach one with query budget, while detect-and-misdirect yields bounded asymptotic ASR; CMPE reduces estimated ASR upper bounds by up to two orders of magnitude.
conclusion: Defensive misdirection is a promising strategy to mitigate automated jailbreak attacks, significantly reducing attack success rates.

title: Efficient And Sound Probabilistic Verification For Ai Agents
authors: Alaia Solko-Breslin, Pramod Kaushik Mudrakarta, Mihai Christodorescu, Somesh Jha, Krishnamurthy Dj Dvijotham
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Securing AI agents that operate in complex digital environments has become a critical need, and runtime monitoring approaches that formulate and enforce policies expressed in a formal language like Datalog offer a promising solution. However, existing approaches are restricted to deterministic policies. In many practical applications of AI agents, there is a need to enforce security policies in the face of ambiguity, leading to probabilistic predicates or state transitions (for example, a declassifier or Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detector that has some failure probability on each invocation). Furthermore, in many such applications, one cannot easily make the independence assumptions necessary to invoke prior work on probabilistic inference in Datalog. We address this by introducing a sound and efficient framework for such verification based on distributionally robust optimization, computing sound upper bounds on the probability of policy violation regardless of possible correlations between predicates. On standard benchmarks for terminal and tool calling agents, we demonstrate that our approach outperforms prior art and improves the security-utility trade-off while ensuring rigorous bounds on the probability of policy violation.
tldr: This paper presents a sound and efficient probabilistic verification framework for AI agents using distributionally robust optimization to bound policy violation probabilities.
motivation: Existing runtime monitoring approaches for AI agents are restricted to deterministic policies, but many practical applications require enforcing security policies under probabilistic predicates or state transitions without independence assumptions.
method: The authors formulate the verification problem as distributionally robust optimization, computing sound upper bounds on the probability of policy violation that hold regardless of correlations between predicates.
result: On standard benchmarks for terminal and tool calling agents, the approach outperforms prior art and improves the security-utility trade-off while ensuring rigorous bounds on violation probability.
conclusion: The framework enables efficient and sound probabilistic verification for AI agents, addressing a critical need in securing AI systems operating in complex environments.

title: Functional Completeness And Primitive Positive Decomposition Of Relations On Finite Domains
authors: Sergiy Koshkin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new and elementary construction of primitive positive decomposition of higher arity relations into binary relations on finite domains. Such decompositions come up in applications to constraint satisfaction problems, clone theory and relational databases. The construction exploits functional completeness of 2-input functions in many-valued logic by interpreting relations as graphs of partially defined multivalued 'functions'. The 'functions' are then composed from ordinary functions in the usual sense. The construction is computationally effective and relies on well-developed methods of functional decomposition, but reduces relations only to ternary relations. An additional construction then decomposes ternary into binary relations, also effectively, by converting certain disjunctions into existential quantifications. The result gives a uniform proof of Peirce's reduction thesis on finite domains, and shows that the graph of any Sheffer function composes all relations there.
tldr: The paper presents a new construction for decomposing higher-arity relations into binary relations on finite domains using functional completeness in many-valued logic.
motivation: To provide an elementary and effective method for primitive positive decomposition of relations, with applications to constraint satisfaction, clone theory, and relational databases.
method: Interprets relations as graphs of partially defined multivalued functions and composes them from ordinary functions using functional completeness of 2-input functions; then reduces ternary to binary relations via existential quantifications.
result: The construction yields a uniform proof of Peirce's reduction thesis on finite domains and shows that the graph of any Sheffer function composes all relations.
conclusion: The work offers a computationally effective decomposition method and contributes to the theoretical understanding of relation composition on finite domains.

result: The framework retains interpretability while incorporating essential physics, enabling more accurate modeling of flow in fractured porous media.
conclusion: The proposed global Buckley-Leverett theory provides a practical tool for simulating multicomponent flow in fractured reservoirs with improved physical fidelity.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights can help improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is key for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Summarizes recent gravitational-wave detections from binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical nuclear equation of state models.
result: Provides constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and compares them to predictions from nuclear theory.
conclusion: Neutron star observations offer unique insights into dense matter, but further data are needed to discriminate between equation of state models.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; this review surveys three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined approaches for a complete defect picture.
result: The paper summarizes capabilities and limitations of each technique and highlights cases where combining them yields more comprehensive disorder characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods, especially when combined, provide direct access to atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors, aiding materials understanding.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics but experimentally challenging due to low rates.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state-of-the-art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory and experimental techniques.
conclusion: The paper is a comprehensive review of nuclear astrophysics, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, focusing on the generation and use of maximally localized Wannier functions.
result: It describes the ecosystem's capabilities for computing band structures, topological invariants, and other properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling accurate and insightful materials simulations.

title: Electron Spin Drift In Long-distance Plasma Wakefield Acceleration
authors: Ming Zeng And Dazhang Li Yilan Guo
abstract: Plasma based wakefield acceleration of polarized electron beams has recently attracted considerable research interest. Previous works have found the forced spin oscillation of electrons due to two-dimensional betatron oscillation in particle trajectory and discovered longitudinal depolarization mechanism in plasma wakefield. In this work, we present a three-dimensional analytical model for the electron spin dynamics and derive the evolution of polarization during long-distance plasma wakefield acceleration. Our analysis reveals several phenomena including a transverse rotational spin drift leading to depolarization, a reversal of the drift frequency, and a consequent recovery of polarization. This work can offer guidance on future plasma-based accelerators for polarized electron beams.
tldr: This paper presents a three-dimensional analytical model for electron spin dynamics in plasma wakefield acceleration, focusing on spin drift and depolarization.
motivation: Polarized electron beams are important for high-energy physics, but spin dynamics in plasma accelerators are not well understood, especially over long distances.
method: The authors develop a 3D analytical model for electron spin evolution during plasma wakefield acceleration, incorporating betatron oscillations and longitudinal fields.
result: They find a transverse rotational spin drift that causes depolarization, a reversal of drift frequency, and a subsequent recovery of polarization.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for designing plasma-based accelerators that preserve electron beam polarization.

title: Networks Of Agglomeration: How Population Density Rewires Social Networks And Reshapes Contagion Dynamics
authors: Christopher K. Tokita
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From ancient Mesopotamia to modern cities, dense human settlements coincide with bursts of economic productivity, cultural innovation, and social change. But how does packing people more tightly together alter social organization in ways that reshape collective outcomes? Here, I use a minimal agent-based model to isolate the effect of population density, holding population size and individual behavior fixed while varying only how closely individuals are placed in space. In the model, individuals form social ties gradually, favoring those nearby and those already well-connected. Under these simple rules, varying population density alone is sufficient to reorganize social network structure: sparse populations develop locally clustered communities, while denser ones form globally integrated networks with shorter social distances and a tightly interconnected core of popular individuals. This structural transition occurs sharply over a narrow range of densities and is governed by whether physical proximity or social popularity dominates tie formation. Simulating contagions on these networks reveals that the consequences of this shift depend on what is spreading. Simple contagions (e.g., information or disease) reach a majority of individuals more quickly in denser populations. Complex contagions (e.g., social norms or collective behaviors) do not spread faster, but instead achieve broader and more reliable adoption as density increases. Together, these results show that population density can act as a structural force independent of the economic and behavioral mechanisms typically invoked to explain why cities are engines of change.
tldr: This paper uses an agent-based model to study how population density rewires social networks and affects contagion dynamics, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To isolate the effect of population density on social network structure and collective outcomes, independent of economic or behavioral factors.
method: A minimal agent-based model where individuals form social ties based on proximity and popularity, varying only population density.
result: Sparse populations yield clustered communities; dense populations yield globally integrated networks with a core of popular individuals. Simple contagions spread faster in dense populations; complex contagions achieve broader adoption.
conclusion: Population density alone can reorganize social networks and reshape contagion dynamics, acting as a structural force in cities.

title: Narrative Structure In Tropes: A Computational Analysis Of `Friends'
authors: Shun Zhang, Tabia Tanzin Prama, Christopher M. Danforth, Peter Sheridan Dodds
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tropes are recurring narrative devices in television and film. We carry out a computational analysis of tropes in the sitcom Friends, using human-curated trope annotations from TVTropes, episode transcripts, and IMDb ratings. Because automatic trope detection remains challenging, we treat existing trope annotations as a curated analytical layer and focus on their downstream narrative and semantic functions. We first examine the relationship between episode-level trope frequency and audience reception. We find a statistically significant positive association between trope count and weighted IMDb ratings, although the modest explanatory power suggests that more than trope density alone explains audience evaluation. We then connect trope annotations to dialogue transcripts and represent trope-related dialogue using TF-IDF-based semantic features. Using PCA and k-means clustering, we group 1,954 distinct tropes into 15 semantically interpretable clusters. Chi-square analyses show that the six main characters are unevenly distributed across these clusters, with character-specific trope profiles that are broadly consistent with their established narrative identities. Finally, we project trope clusters into the ousiometric power-danger space to examine their semantic organization. The results show that "Physical and Sexual Comedy" occupies a region associated with relatively high danger, while "Revelation, Surprise, and Reaction" occupies a region associated with relatively high power. Overall, our work demonstrates a way to operationalize trope measurement and shows that identifiable trope clusters can provide holistic "distant reading" descriptions of characters and stories.
tldr: A computational analysis of narrative tropes in the TV show Friends using human-curated annotations, dialogue transcripts, and IMDb ratings.
motivation: To understand how tropes function narratively and semantically, and to explore their relationship with audience reception and character identity.
method: Statistical analysis of trope frequency vs. IMDb ratings; TF-IDF feature extraction from dialogue; PCA and k-means clustering of tropes; chi-square tests for character-trope associations; projection into ousiometric space.
result: Positive correlation between trope count and ratings; 15 semantic clusters identified; characters have distinct trope profiles; clusters map to power-danger semantic space.
conclusion: Trope measurement can be operationalized and provides a 'distant reading' of narrative structure and character roles.

title: Methodological Guidelines For Circadian Modeling Of Daylight Saving Time: Application To The United States
authors: Jorge Mira Jose Maria Martin-Olalla
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling the circadian impact of seasonal clock changing requires precise synchronization between solar and social time. This report critiques a recent study that associated disease prevalence in the United States with seasonal clock exposure. We identify a fundamental computational error in which a sign reversal of the longitudinal offset effectively inverted the US East-West axis, cross-correlating local health data with the circadian burden of hypothetical locations on the opposite side of a time zone. We outline the methodology for a correct modelization of the circadian process in the context of US geography.
tldr: This paper critiques a circadian modeling study of daylight saving time in the US, correcting a sign error in longitudinal offset.
motivation: To correct a computational error in a previous study that associated disease prevalence with seasonal clock exposure, which inverted the US East-West axis.
method: The authors identify a sign reversal in the longitudinal offset calculation and outline a correct methodology for modeling circadian impact using US geography.
result: The previous study's results are invalid due to the sign error; the correct methodology is provided.
conclusion: Proper synchronization of solar and social time is essential for accurate circadian modeling of daylight saving time effects.

title: A Four-Section Bracket For The 48-team World Cup
authors: Chong Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The expansion of the FIFA World Cup to 48 teams in 2026 introduces structural challenges in tournament design. To populate a 32-team knockout bracket from 12 groups of four, the current FIFA rules select the eight best third-placed teams using a global ranking across all groups. This global coupling creates several major problems: a combinatorial explosion of 495 possible bracket configurations; a fundamentally biased and unequal selection of third-placed qualifiers; lack of a clear path for group winners; vulnerability to collusion and ranking manipulation; and no guarantee of same-group separation beyond the first knockout round. We propose a simple unified solution called the four-section bracket (FSB) rule: split the 12 groups into four sections of three groups. All group winners, runners-up, and the two best third-placed teams in each section advance. Group winners remain in their home sections as local anchors, while lower-ranked qualifiers are transferred to other sections according to a fixed, symmetric rule. This structure guarantees same-group separation until the semifinal, protects the top eight group winners with a predictable knockout path, and reduces bracket complexity from 495 configurations to just one invariant topology per section, recovering the symmetry of the traditional 32-team format. We show substantial improvements in competitive fairness and scheduling predictability.
tldr: This paper proposes a bracket design for the 48-team FIFA World Cup, focusing on tournament fairness and scheduling.
motivation: The expansion to 48 teams introduces structural challenges and biases in the current qualification system.
method: The authors propose a four-section bracket rule that splits groups into sections and uses a fixed transfer rule for lower-ranked teams.
result: The new bracket reduces complexity from 495 configurations to one invariant topology per section and guarantees same-group separation until the semifinal.
conclusion: The four-section bracket improves competitive fairness and scheduling predictability over the current FIFA rules.

title: Have Data Centers Raised Your Electric Bill? Causal Evidence From The United States
authors: Asa Watten, John Bistline, Geoffrey Blanford
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We estimate that data centers caused average retail electricity rates to fall modestly in the United States from 2015 to 2024 using an instrumental variables approach. Despite prevailing sentiment, the finding is consistent with economic reasoning: existing large power system fixed costs, economies of scale in transmission and distribution, and declining unit costs for generation imply that durable demand growth lowers average prices. We find patterns of economies of scale for transmission, distribution, and generation costs as well as within and across retail customer classes. We caution that future supply constraints could reverse the effect.
tldr: This paper studies the causal effect of data centers on retail electricity rates in the US, finding a modest decrease due to economies of scale.
motivation: To empirically test the common belief that data centers increase electricity costs for consumers.
method: Uses an instrumental variables approach with data from 2015-2024 to estimate the impact of data center demand on average retail electricity rates.
result: Data centers caused average retail electricity rates to fall modestly, contrary to prevailing sentiment.
conclusion: Durable demand growth from data centers can lower average prices due to economies of scale, but future supply constraints could reverse this effect.

title: Mid-infrared Photothermal Imaging Flow Cytometry
authors: Yusei Sugawara, Keiichiro Toda, Genki Ishigane, Masato Fukushima, Takuro Ideguchi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Imaging flow cytometry (IFC) enables high-throughput single-cell analysis but largely relies on fluorescence labeling to obtain molecular specificity. Label-free vibrational imaging can provide intrinsic chemical contrast, yet coherent Raman-based methods interrogate only a limited axial volume, which restricts quantitative whole-cell analysis under flow. Mid-infrared photothermal (MIP) microscopy offers a promising route to overcome this limitation by combining linear mid-infrared (MIR) absorption-based chemical contrast with visible-light detection, allowing chemical imaging of a broader axial volume of each cell in a wide-field configuration. However, applying MIP microscopy to rapidly flowing cells has been difficult because conventional frame-sequential acquisition of MIR-ON and MIR-OFF images is highly susceptible to motion-induced subtraction artifacts. Here we demonstrate MIP-IFC, a label-free imaging flow cytometry platform based on single-shot nanosecond-dual-pulse MIP (SNAP-MIP) microscopy. SNAP-MIP encodes the MIR-ON and MIR-OFF states into separate holographic channels within a single camera exposure, reducing their temporal separation to 20 ns. This single-shot acquisition suppresses motion artifacts and increases the allowable sample velocity for artifact-free MIP imaging by five orders of magnitude compared with conventional frame-sequential MIP imaging. Leveraging this capability, MIP-IFC acquired chemical images at 500 frames per second and achieved a cellular event rate up to ~70 events s^-1. We demonstrate quantitative chemical discrimination of flowing microbeads and apply MIP-IFC to single-cell profiling of oleic-acid-induced lipid accumulation, adipocyte differentiation, and confluence-dependent cellular heterogeneity. These results establish MIP-IFC as a high-throughput, quantitative, label-free chemical imaging platform for single-cell phenotyping under flow.
tldr: This paper presents a label-free imaging flow cytometry platform using mid-infrared photothermal microscopy with single-shot dual-pulse acquisition to achieve high-throughput chemical imaging of single cells.
motivation: Imaging flow cytometry typically relies on fluorescence labeling for molecular specificity, which can perturb cells. Label-free vibrational imaging methods like coherent Raman have limited axial volume, hindering quantitative whole-cell analysis under flow.
method: The authors developed SNAP-MIP microscopy, which encodes mid-infrared ON and OFF states into separate holographic channels within a single camera exposure (20 ns temporal separation), enabling artifact-free imaging at 500 frames per second.
result: The platform achieved a cellular event rate of ~70 events/s and demonstrated quantitative chemical discrimination of microbeads and single-cell profiling of lipid accumulation and adipocyte differentiation.
conclusion: MIP-IFC establishes a high-throughput, label-free chemical imaging platform for single-cell phenotyping under flow, with potential applications in biology and medicine.

title: Multiparameter $C$-semigroups And Multiparameter $C$-cosine Functions
authors: Marko Kostic, Halis Can Koyuncuoglu, Youssef N. Raffoul
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present several new results concerning multiparameter [MATH]-semigroups. We introduce and systematically analyze the class of multiparameter [MATH]-cosine functions, providing several new structural results and applications to abstract multiparameter Cauchy problems of first/second order in locally convex spaces. We also consider automatic extensions of multiparameter [MATH]-semigroups and multiparameter [MATH]-cosine functions.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes multiparameter C-semigroups and C-cosine functions in locally convex spaces, with applications to abstract Cauchy problems.
motivation: To extend the theory of one-parameter operator semigroups to multiparameter settings and provide structural results for C-cosine functions.
method: The authors define multiparameter C-semigroups and C-cosine functions, prove structural properties, and apply them to first- and second-order Cauchy problems in locally convex spaces.
result: New structural results for multiparameter C-cosine functions and automatic extensions of multiparameter C-semigroups are obtained.
conclusion: The work contributes to abstract operator theory and functional analysis, with potential applications to partial differential equations.

title: On The Family Of Measurable Sets Having The Upper Positive Density
authors: Jacek Hejduk, Renata Wiertelak, W{\l}adys{\l}aw Wilczy\'nski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The essence of the density topology lies in the family of Lebesgue measurable sets where each point of a set is a density point of that set. The motivation of this work is to investigate the family of measurable sets for which, at every point within a set belonging to this family, the upper density of that set is positive. We obtain a strong generalized topology, and its essential properties are demonstrated in comparison with those of the classical density topology.
tldr: This paper studies a family of measurable sets with positive upper density and constructs a strong generalized topology, comparing it to the classical density topology.
motivation: To investigate measurable sets where every point has positive upper density, extending the concept of density topology.
method: The authors define a new family of sets and prove it forms a strong generalized topology, analyzing its properties relative to the classical density topology.
result: A new strong generalized topology is obtained, with essential properties demonstrated and compared to the classical density topology.
conclusion: The family of sets with positive upper density yields a topology with distinct properties, contributing to measure theory and topology.

title: A Proof Of The Avkhadiev-Wirths Conjecture On Brezis-Marcus Constants
authors: R. G. Nasibullin I. I. Gabdulkhalikov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we deal with geometrical versions of Hardy type inequalities with additional positive terms in convex domains. The constant [MATH] multiplying the additional term depends on the geometry of the multidimensional domain [MATH] and the numerical parameters of the problem. The constant (functional) [MATH] is called Brezis-Marcus constant. In 2010, F.G. Avkhadiev and K.-J. Wirths proposed the hypothesis that among all [MATH]-dimensional domains with given inradius the maximum of the best Brezis-Marcus constant is achieved for the [MATH]-dimensional ball of radius. Using one dimensional Hardy type inequalities we proved the Avkhadiev-Wirths conjecture on Brezis-Marcus constants in the cases [MATH] and [MATH]. The sharp constants are solutions of the equation in terms of special functions and fixed eigenvalues of the Sturm-Liouville differential operators. The corresponding eigenfunctions in the [MATH]-d case are spheroidal wave functions and for dimensions greater than or equal to [MATH] are confluent Heun functions. New properties of the Heun functions are established and their zeros are found. We provide Python code for calculating sharp constants.

motivation: The authors aim to prove the Avkhadiev-Wirths conjecture about the maximum of Brezis-Marcus constants in convex domains, which is a problem in classical analysis and PDEs.
method: The proof uses one-dimensional Hardy-type inequalities and reduces the problem to solving eigenvalue equations for Sturm-Liouville operators, involving spheroidal wave functions and confluent Heun functions.
result: The conjecture is proved for dimensions n=2 and n≥3, with sharp constants expressed in terms of special functions, and Python code is provided for numerical computation.
conclusion: The work resolves a conjecture in geometric Hardy inequalities, contributing to classical analysis but not to the user's research areas.

title: Duality For Interpolation Spaces Defined Via Slowly Varying Functions: The Case 0<q<1
authors: P. Fern\'andez-Mart\'inez, M. Grover, T. M. Signes
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given [MATH] a compatible couple of Banach spaces, we describe the dual of the limiting real interpolation space [MATH] for [MATH] and [MATH] a slowly varying function. In the process, we use the [MATH]-spaces [MATH] and we establish an equivalence theorem for [MATH] and [MATH] spaces of independent interest. result: Describes the dual of limiting real interpolation spaces and recovers known results as examples.

title: On $h=w$ In Banach Function Spaces
authors: \c{s}eyma \c{c}etin, David Cruz-Uribe OFS, Scott Rodney

title: On The Limits Of Biased Derivative Information For Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization
authors: Brian Bullins Anant Shyam
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of finding [MATH]-stationary points for [MATH], i.e., [MATH] such that [MATH], for smooth, non-convex objectives, where the derivative oracles are not only stochastic but also biased. In the first-order setting, we provide tight lower bounds for finding an [MATH]-stationary point, for [MATH] and where [MATH] is a bound on the gradient bias, matching the upper bounds of Ajalloeian and Stich (2020). We then establish bias-dependent lower bounds for algorithms that use higher-order derivative information for finding [MATH]-stationary points, where [MATH] is a bound on the maximum bias for all derivatives. To complement these lower bounds, we develop trust-region based methods that, for certain ranges of bias, provide guarantees that match the corresponding lower bounds. We further improve upon the oracle complexity in high bias settings through a higher-order variance reduction scheme, in particular demonstrating the benefits, in some cases, of using higher-order derivative information, whereas such improvements are known to be unattainable for stochastic unbiased settings.

motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of optimization with biased gradient information is important for practical machine learning, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors derive tight lower bounds for first-order and higher-order biased oracles, and propose trust-region and variance-reduction algorithms that match these bounds.

conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the limits of biased derivative information for nonconvex optimization, but it is purely in classical optimization theory.

title: Concave Kite Central Configurations In The Planar Four-Body Problem With Three Equal Masses
authors: Zhifu Xie Yangshanshan Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a complete classification of concave kite central configurations in the planar 4-body problem with three equal masses. There are two different types of central configurations when the fourth mass lies inside or outside the triangle formed by the other three. Using a rigorous computer-assisted analytical method and a fixed coordinate system, we show that the central configurations in each case form a one-parameter family and obtain a complete classification of these configurations. In addition, we rigorously show the existence and types of the bifurcation points in the reduced space. We also provide two numerical global bifurcation pictures in the entire planar 4-body configuration space as the mass ratio varies from [MATH] to [MATH], including symmetric and asymmetric concave central configurations with three equal masses.
tldr: This paper classifies concave kite central configurations in the planar four-body problem with three equal masses using computer-assisted analytical methods.
motivation: Central configurations are important in celestial mechanics for understanding the dynamics of n-body systems, but this work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a rigorous computer-assisted analytical method with a fixed coordinate system to classify configurations and identify bifurcation points.
result: They show that concave kite central configurations form one-parameter families and provide a complete classification, including bifurcation analysis.
conclusion: The classification is complete for the planar four-body problem with three equal masses, but the work has no connection to the user's research interests.

Let [MATH] be a closed linear subspace of the Banach space [MATH] defined with respect to a probability measure [MATH] on [MATH]. We prove that if [MATH] is continuously (identically) embedded into [MATH] for [MATH], then its dimension [MATH] satisfies the estimate \[ {N}\left(,\Gamma!\left({2}\right)}{\Gamma!\left({2}\right)\Gamma!\left({2}\right)}\right)^{2/\tilde q}\le K_{p,q(m)}^2, \] where [MATH], [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH], and [MATH] is a bounded constant. title: Bregman-projected Mirror Methods For Regularized Stationary Mean-field Games
authors: Hussain Al Abdulaziz, Yuri Ashrafyan, Yeva Gevorgyan, Diogo Gomes
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze a Bregman-projected mirror iteration for low-order regularizations of stationary mean-field game (MFG) systems in their natural Banach space setting. For separable Hamiltonians of the form \(H(x,p,m)=H_0(x,p)-g(m)\), with quadratic or super-quadratic Hamiltonian growth and linear or super-linear density couplings, we formulate a low-order \(\bar\gamma\)-Laplacian regularization of the stationary MFG system as a variational inequality on \(L^{\bar\beta}(\mathbb T^d)\times W^{1,\bar\gamma}(\mathbb T^d)\). To approximate solutions of this regularized variational inequality, we introduce a Bregman geometry matched to the mixed Lebesgue--Sobolev exponents of the problem and analyze a constrained two-step mirror method with frozen operator evaluation. For the exact constrained iteration and each fixed regularization parameter \(\epsi>0\), we derive a one-step Bregman inequality and use it to prove that the constrained iteration converges strongly to the unique solution of the regularized variational inequality under natural summability conditions on the step sizes. Numerical experiments on one- and two-dimensional models, validated against exact test solutions, illustrate residual decay under mesh refinement and suggest improved practical performance of the two-step implementation in the tested discretizations.
tldr: This paper develops Bregman-projected mirror methods for solving regularized stationary mean-field game systems, a topic in applied mathematics and game theory.
motivation: Mean-field games model large populations of interacting agents; solving them efficiently is important for economics and social sciences.
method: The authors formulate a low-order Laplacian regularization as a variational inequality and propose a constrained two-step mirror method with Bregman geometry tailored to the function spaces.
result: They prove strong convergence of the iteration to the unique solution under summability conditions and demonstrate residual decay in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a convergent and numerically effective approach for regularized stationary mean-field games.

title: On A Class Of Modified Cayley--Magnus Methods
authors: Sergio Blanes, Fernando Casas, Arieh Iserles
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new class of numerical integrators for the time integration of non-autonomous linear ordinary differential equations whose coefficient matrix is sparse and evolves within a quadratic matrix Lie group. In contrast to standard Lie group integrators, the proposed methods avoid the evaluation of matrix exponentials acting on vectors and instead rely on solving a sequence of linear systems with sparse coefficient matrices. Moreover, they are well suited for problems arising from unbounded operators, as they inherently produce bounded solutions. We construct optimised schemes of orders four and six and assess their performance on a representative numerical example, demonstrating clear advantages over existing Lie-group integrators.
tldr: This paper introduces a new class of numerical integrators for non-autonomous linear ODEs with sparse coefficient matrices evolving in quadratic matrix Lie groups.
motivation: Standard Lie group integrators require evaluating matrix exponentials, which is computationally expensive for large sparse systems. The authors aim to develop methods that avoid exponentials and are suitable for unbounded operators.
method: The proposed methods replace matrix exponentials with solving sequences of linear systems with sparse coefficient matrices, leveraging the quadratic Lie group structure. Optimized schemes of orders four and six are constructed.
result: The new integrators produce bounded solutions for problems with unbounded operators and show clear advantages over existing Lie-group integrators in a numerical example.
